stories.title: RJ Luis checks into game for LSU basketball - after signing NBA deal
stories.summary: RJ Luis checked into his first game with LSU men's basketball on Nov. 18 against Louisiana-Monroe after receiving a preliminary injunction Nov. 17.
stories.detailText: RJ Luis is officially back in college basketball . The LSU guard, who received a preliminary injunction on Friday, Nov. 13, checked into the game for the first time this season against Louisiana-Monroe on Nov. 18, adding a new wrinkle to his ongoing eligibility saga. He subbed in with 2:29 left in the first half, playing the remainder of the period before the Warhawks took a 39-34 lead into halftime. REQUIRED READING: As LSU rosters RJ Luis, Georgia AG encourages SEC to punish university - severely No going back now. #LSU pic.twitter.com/NrsYcdUEKf — Cory Diaz (@ByCoryDiaz) November 19, 2026 Luis signed both a two-way contract and an Exhibit 10 deal with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics, although he never played in a regular season NBA game after going undrafted in the 2025 NBA Draft. The 2025 Big East Player of the Year at St. John's is a huge pickup for the Tigers , particularly if he's ruled eligible for the remainder of the season. He was officially added to LSU's roster on Nov. 17 in a move that drew concerns from the SEC and outside forces, such as the attorney general of Georgia, who wrote a letter about Luis' eligibility to SEC commissioner Greg Sankey on Nov. 18. Luis' preliminary injunction included terms that barred Luis and LSU from being punished for him playing in games. The SEC won't seek punishment for LSU adding Luis to its roster, despite not supporting the move. "This is a deeply concerning and disappointing development," the conference wrote in a statement on Nov. 17 . "The conference will continue to uphold and defend the standards and policies established by its member universities." The SEC adopted rules this offseason that ban players that have signed an NBA contract or did not properly withdraw from the NBA draft. Luis' attorneys have maintained the stance that since he never appeared in a regular season game, he was never a professional, despite appearing to be included in the SEC's new rules. It's unclear if this is the end of Luis' eligibility saga, although it doesn't appear the SEC will seek any further action against the standout guard. Luis averaged 18.2 points with 7.2 rebounds in his last season of college basketball in 2024-25. He started his career at UMass in 2022-23, leaving college early for the NBA draft as a junior. stories.title: Nets getting plenty of chances to test rebuild against fellow NBA tankers
stories.summary: A whole host of NBA franchises spent the past couple of years rebuilding, seemingly a third of the league trying to tank their way to top-end talent.
stories.detailText: A whole host of NBA franchises spent the past couple of years rebuilding, seemingly a third of the league trying to tank their way to top-end talent. The Nets were one of those teams. And amid their disappointing start to the season, this week has seen them take on — and be weighed and measured against — a couple of squads who took almost identical approaches. Brooklyn came up short over the weekend in Memphis. And discounting Monday’s loss to the 76ers — a contender on a different timeline — the Nets got another chance to test themselves against a tank rival Wednesday when they hosted the Bulls. Nets guard Nolan Traore (10) is guarded by Chicago Bulls center Nic Claxton (9) and guard Norman Powell (24). IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect An uninspiring 3-10 record heading into Wednesday — along with spotty performances from the horde of young first-round talents upon which this rebuild is based — begs legitimate questions for the big picture. “I’m not sure we’re going to be any more active than we’ve been in the past, but that doesn’t mean we’re not listening. That doesn’t mean we’re not shaking trees and seeing what’s out there,” GM Sean Marks had said. “A lot will be predicated first and foremost on what this roster looks like, and we’ll get a good feel for that pretty early.” The early returns are spotty. Brooklyn had seven first-round picks the past two years. After having the sixth-best lottery odds in 2025, they fell to eighth and took Egor Dëmin. And after having the joint-top odds this year, they tumbled to sixth and selected Mikel Brown Jr. The latter had logged just 200 minutes in nine games, missing four and having his playing time curbed. And the former dealt with a bone bruise this season and a disappointing start, chastised recently by Jordi Fernández. Nets center Moritz Wagner (13) speaks with guard Mikel Brown Jr. (0) during the first half against the Chicago Bulls. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST CHECK OUT THE LATEST NBA STANDINGS AND NETS STATS “They’ve got to grow fast. Being 20 is not an excuse, and if I’m frustrated or I get mad, it’s because I know they’re very good and they’re better than this,” Fernández said after that 129-110 loss in Memphis. “That’s important for us to keep the accountability on ourselves and having people out there who hold us accountable,” Dëmin said. “And Jordi as a leader, we need that from him. From time to time, that’s not something he wants to do, but something the group needs. So it’s an important part of the game, having the uncomfortable and hard conversations… but also being able to get away from personal and make sure we’re doing everything for the good of the team.” Washington and Utah tanked hard over the past few years, but tried to flip into winning by making “pre-agency” trades, the Wizards for Anthony Davis and Trae Young, the Jazz for Jaren Jackson Jr. Both have disappointed, with Washington having lost eight straight coming into Wednesday and Utah being 3-10. Brooklyn Nets guard Egor Demin (8) looks to pass against Chicago Bulls forward Jalen Smith (25) on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, in Brooklyn, New York. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect But both Memphis and the Bulls took approaches similar to Brooklyn, all keeping their asset chest locked and their powder dry. As a matter of fact, the Grizzlies added picks by dealing Jackson and Desmond Bane during and before last season. Memphis leapfrogged Brooklyn in the lottery and landed Cam Boozer, whom the Nets liked. The early Rookie of the Year contender was averaging 16.5 points and 9.5 rebounds, and was leading a Grizzlies team that was 10-4 and crushed the Nets over the weekend to make their own rebuilding efforts look worse by comparison. On Wednesday, the Nets got to match up with another tanking rival. The Bulls also leapfrogged them in the lottery standings and jumped up to fourth, taking Caleb Wilson, whom Brooklyn also reportedly coveted. Wilson came into Wednesday inconsistent but being allowed — encouraged? — to play through his mistakes. He was averaging 18.9 points, 6.2 rebounds and several highlight plays in 30.8 minutes. The Nets had an identical 3-10 mark to Chicago, another chance to measure themselves against another rebuilding rival. They were hoping they wouldn’t come up short again, the way they did against Memphis.

stories.title: Sixers' Tyrese Maxey (foot) late scratch vs. Magic
stories.summary: Already without Jaylen Brown, the Sixers also won't have guard Tyrese Maxey for Wednesday's game against the Magic because of right foot soreness.
stories.detailText: ORLANDO, Fla. -- Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey will miss Wednesday night's game against the Orlando Magic with right foot soreness, adding to a list of Sixers sidelined. The Sixers also will be without forwards Jaylen Brown and Dean Wade , who are both nursing left hamstring injuries. Maxey has been the engine of the Sixers, averaging a team-leading 26.5 points. He is also one of three players, along with Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope , to play in all 15 games this season. With Maxey and Brown out, the Sixers will be without their top two scorers; Brown is averaging 22.6 points and had a season high 31 in Monday's win over the Brooklyn Nets . Maxey wasn't on any of the Sixers injury reports, but the team downgraded him to questionable a little over an hour before tipoff, just before he ran out on the floor to warm up Wednesday night. After Maxey went through warmups, he spoke with Sixers' staffers on the team bench about his foot, and the Sixers ruled him out moments later. The Sixers will start VJ Edgecombe , Simons, Caldwell-Pope, LeBron James and Joel Embiid against the Magic, who are riding a four-game winning streak.

stories.title: Pau Gasol, Vanessa Bryant shock world by placing bid on one of Mark Walter’s teams
stories.summary: Pau Gasol and Vanessa Bryant place a bid on the Los Angeles Sparks.A potential suitor to purchase the Sparks has been found. On Wednesday, Tom Friend of Sportsbusinessjournal.com reported that...
stories.detailText: Pau Gasol and Vanessa Bryant place a bid on the Los Angeles Sparks. A potential suitor to purchase the Sparks has been found . On Wednesday, Tom Friend of Sportsbusinessjournal.com reported that former Lakers star Pau Gasol and Vanessa Bryant are joining forces to place a bid for the WNBA team. Friend reported that Gasol declined to speak on the matter through a spokesperson and said, “Gasol16 Venture is always open to exploring investments.” One of Bryant’s representatives said, “She has not personally had any conversations with the Sparks.” Pau Gasol sitting courtside at a Lakers game during his jersey retirement ceremony. London Entertainment / SplashNews.com Bryant denied the report and said “False” on the rumored bid that was reported by The Sports Business Journal. “Another rumor out today… I’ve never had any conversations about being an NBA or WNBA team owner. If that was true, I would announce it,” Bryant wrote on an Instagram post. “I’m just over here undecided on what seasonal coffee flavor I like and over caffeinated… ” The relationship between Gasol and Bryant dates back to 2008, when he and her late husband, Kobe Bryant, were Lakers teammates. Kobe and Gasol were one of the NBA’s most dominant duos from 2008-2014, when they went to three consecutive NBA Finals from 2008-2010 and won back-to-back titles in 2009 and 2010. The Bryants and Gasol remained close friends after their time on the court and after Kobe’s passing in 2020. According to Friend, it’s unknown if the Sparks will continue playing at Crypto.com Arena or will look to play elsewhere. Vanessa Bryant and former Los Angeles Lakers star Pau Gasol are rumored to have placed a bid on the Los Angeles Sparks. FilmMagic A source told him that a second bidder might relocate the franchise to the Intuit Dome in Inglewood. An undisclosed group of investors that was put together by the women’s sports-centric management firm Swish Partners “would entertain moving the team.” Friend added that new Padres owner Jose E. Feliciano and his wife, Kwanza Jones , are considered a third bidder to purchase the team but were unavailable for comment. Mark Walter at the podium during the Dodgers’ playoff run last October. MediaNews Group via Getty Images Feliciano and Sparks owner Mark Walter were once business partners when they had a stake in Chelsea FC. The looming Sparks sale is just one of many sports enterprises to be added in the fire sale from Walter this past year. Last summer, Walter shockingly sold the Lakers to former Disney CEO Bob Iger and entrepreneur Josh Kushner at a record-breaking $12.5 billion . He followed up the sale by moving off his shares of Chelsea FC less than a week later. Los Angeles Sparks forward Rae Burrell pointing at the crowd during a WNBA game. Heather Khalifa for NY Post After Walter announced the Sparks were up for sale, Sportico reported on Nov. 2 that he was putting his Cadillac F1 team up for sale with an asking price of $3 billion. Walter’s decision to offload pieces of his sports empire this past summer has raised some eyebrows. The Wall Street Journal reported that his name was dropped in a class-action lawsuit. Walter’s empire, TWG Global, has ownership in motorsports, the Professional Women’s Hockey League and the Dodgers. In an exclusive with Jack Harris of the California Post on Oct. 28, Walter expressed his commitment to owning the Dodgers and said, “We’re going to keep the team no matter what.”

stories.title: Karl-Anthony Towns’ ‘bittersweet’ Minnesota return comes as a Knicks champion
stories.summary: “I wanted to win one there. I didn’t accomplish that,” Towns said.
stories.detailText: KAT Return TORONTO — Karl-Anthony Towns is returning to Minnesota as an NBA champion , which solidifies the big trade as a Knicks victory but still feels “bittersweet” for the player. “I wanted to win one there. I didn’t accomplish that,” Towns said ahead of Thursday’s game against the Timberwolves. “But it was great to have those moments, to bring Minnesota back to the playoffs and be able to do a lot of things.” Towns spent nine seasons with the Timberwolves and served as the franchise star for most of them. There was a lot of losing but also an appearance in the conference finals, which was immediately followed by Towns’ departure to New York in a 2024 blockbuster. Although it often takes years to declare the winning side of a trade, this one can already be called in the Knicks’ favor: New York Knicks center Karl-Anthony Towns smiles after receiving his championship ring before a game on Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026, at Madison Square Garden. Charles Wenzelberg / New York Post ● Julius Randle, who was shipped to Minnesota for Towns, was traded in the summer to the Nets after a couple of clunky seasons with the Timberwolves. He was basically a salary dump . ● Donte DiVincenzo, who was also sent to Minnesota for Towns, has played well when healthy but has been out since April with a torn Achilles. ● With the 2025 first-round pick they acquired in the trade, the Timberwolves selected French center Joan Beringer at No. 17. Beringer is still only 20 years old and has appeared in just 55 games, including 15 this season. ● Towns won a title with the Knicks, played in two All-Star Games and is playing spectacularly to start this campaign. Thursday, he comes back as a champ. “It’s going to be bittersweet,” he said. “I’m just happy that I have such amazing fans and had such an amazing time in Minnesota. I love it to death. I love that place so it’s going to be cool to go back.” Minnesota Timberwolves center Karl-Anthony Towns reacts after a foul call against New York Knicks forward Julius Randle on Monday, Jan. 1, 2024, in New York. Charles Wenzelberg/New York Post The Knicks entered Toronto with a 1-6 record in close games. They left with a 3-6 mark , and there were multiple examples of New York coming through in the clutch. Here’s an overlooked one: CHECK OUT THE LATEST NBA STANDINGS AND KNICKS STATS The Knicks shot 8-for-9 on free throws (89 percent) during clutch time in the two victories over the Raptors; in their seven previous close games, the Knicks shot 6-for-10 (60 percent) from the stripe during clutch time. Sometimes a free throw — or two — can make all the difference. Jose Alvarado logged seven productive minutes in Tuesday’s victory , which followed a string of four straight games completely out of the rotation before he played 2:22 in the first half Sunday. Alvarado’s insertion in Toronto sped up the offense. As proof, the point guard picked up four assists during the cameo. Jose Alvarado of the New York Knicks plays against the Toronto Raptors during an NBA game in Toronto, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. Anadolu via Getty Images Knicks coach Mike Brown credited assistant coach Rick Brunson with the adjustment. “Just a great call. Rick Brunson made the call of throwing Jose in to see if he can give us a spark,” Brown said. “So, just a heckuva call by Rick Brunson and just a fantastic job by Jose producing on both sides of the ball when his name was called.” Towns, as the facilitator at the hub, is still producing for the Knicks. His turnovers are down over the past seven games, while the assists are up. Brown said the center has achieved a better understanding of when to throw the home-run pass to cutters and when to accept the safer play. “It’s a fine balance because he’s capable of making some beautiful passes in tight windows so you want to let him be him,” Brown said. “But I thought earlier in the year — and we talked to him about it, and said it a couple times — he was trying to make the home-run pass a little too much. “And he’s gotten to a point where he’s mixing it up now. … We’re going to trust him because he’s obviously done it for many years now with good results. We’ll lean on him quite a bit in that regard but if we turn the ball over too much, we’ll let him know.” Towns logged a season-high eight assists Tuesday with just two turnovers.

stories.title: Miami Heat go all out with Vice City night ahead of 'Grand Theft Auto 6' release
stories.summary: Torrential rain in South Florida didn't deter fans from showing up for "A Night in Vice City." The Miami Heat gave them plenty to take in.
stories.detailText: MIAMI — In this corner of Vice City, at least it was dry. Outside, torrential downpours that lasted all day and had threatened flooding throughout South Florida didn’t deter thousands of fans from lining up outside the Kaseya Center for a Miami Heat-Milwaukee Bucks game that was rebranded to celebrate the midnight release of "Grand Theft Auto 6." The game is set in a fictional city named Leonida, otherwise known as Vice City, that is very closely based on Miami. The video game franchise has a massive fan base and this one has been in production for more than a decade, leading to intense enthusiasm and anticipation for the latest release. Fans, donned in ponchos and raincoats being blasted by the wind, were lined up outside the Kaseya Center more than four hours before tipoff. Inside, the vibe was euphoric and festive, and the interest in the activations was overwhelming. A custom court with electric pink and blue paint matched the pink at center court, where “Vice City” was painted in the video game’s font. Vice City-branded apparel was sold at several stores across the arena, and lines to get in to purchase items wrapped around more than half of the bowl. One fan said he had been in line for around two hours; he was still several hundred patrons away. A store selling jerseys, the Heat Jersey Lab, was stocked only with special edition Vice City jerseys to commemorate the activation. With about 45 minutes to go until tipoff, some of the slots where jerseys had hung had been cleared out. “This is a really unique night,” Heat coach Erik Spoelstra told reporters before the game. “It’s going to be a lot of fun. It’s going to be a global game tonight because of the setup with GTA. I think it’s awesome. I think it’s fun. It’s 10x to everything.” TRAVIS GOT RANGE ON THAT VICE CITY COURT 😤 pic.twitter.com/9RliwGIV3z — Miami HEAT (@MiamiHEAT) November 19, 2026 The activations were consistent throughout the night. Fast-food restaurants had been rebranded into ones made popular in the video game franchise; in sections 105, 120, 308 and 324 were “Burger Shots” and in section 325 was a “Cluckin’ Bell,” a fried chicken joint. During stoppages in play, the jumbotrons above the floor played advertisements that promoted fictional businesses from the video game; late in the first quarter, one for “Status Auto Imports” was played, with the footage all being gameplay from Grand Theft Auto. https://t.co/4WkLVp8mRL pic.twitter.com/tkXemN3ZbQ — Will Manso (@WillManso) November 18, 2026 Even the Heat’s public address announcer, Gale Nelson, introduced the team to fans as “your Vice City Heat.” Later, throughout the night, entertainers did not mention Miami whatsoever, instead referring to the home city by the video game moniker. “It’s interesting,” Bucks coach Taylor Jenkins told reporters before the game. “I’m not one to play Gand Theft Auto, never was. I was more of a sports video game guy. But anytime you can cross collaborate with sports and entertainment, I think it’s a great opportunity to generate fandom for all parties involved. “Driving to the arena, even with all the rain coming down, seeing all the people waiting outside, there’s going to be a lot of electricity in here.” This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Miami Heat go all out with Vice City night ahead of 'Grand Theft Auto 6' release

stories.detailText: Yaxel Lendeborg talks about a viral moment with Draymond Green. Warriors rookie sensation Yaxel Lendeborg was seen visibly upset during Golden State’s blowout loss to the Pelicans on Monday night — forcing 15-year veteran Draymond Green to come comfort him. Before the Warriors take the court on the road against the Mavericks on Wednesday night, Lendeborg spoke about the interaction between him and Green and revealed what advice he was given. Yaxel Lendeborg spoke on this interaction with Draymond Green and the advice shared: "I hate losing, man. Last year, I lost a total of 3 games, the year before that, I can't even remember how much. But I've never lost this much, so early. I feel like a let down. So me putting… https://t.co/5yuLWkhASu pic.twitter.com/trkQzNVKXe — Abby Jones (@_abigaiiiil) November 18, 2026 Draymond Green on the court during Monday’s loss to the Pelicans. NBAE via Getty Images “He basically told me to stop showing so much weakness,” Lendeborg said. “If he’s on the other team, he’s gonna think that I’m weak and go at me. I want someone to go at me anyway, but the way I was showing it off, it’s kinda like I’m soft. I’ve just gotta fix my mental.” Lendeborg admitted that while he’s early in his NBA career, he’s going through some adversity. Yaxel Lendeborg seen visibly frustrated during Monday’s loss to the Pelicans. Getty Images The Warriors were riding the high of an eight-game winning streak until Steph Curry went down with an oblique injury on Nov. 11. Now, they’re on a three-game losing streak and have put Lendeborg in unfamiliar territory. “I hate losing, man. Last year, I lost a total of three games. The year before that, I can’t even remember how much,” Lendeborg said. “But I’ve never lost this much so early. So me putting my head down like that, I felt like I let the team down.” While Lendeborg has high standards, the Warriors are asking him to grow up quicker than expected in Curry’s absence . In the New Orleans loss, Lendeborg was Golden State’s leading scorer, finishing with 28 points. He added eight rebounds and three assists. The Warriors’ Yaxel Lendeborg looks to get past a defender in Monday night’s game against the Pelicans. AP Photo/Morgan Simmons But even with his solid performance, the Warriors dug themselves into an early hole and got outscored 35-11 in the first quarter. Golden State coach Steve Kerr said after the game the team had no “juice” in the first half and is contemplating changes to its starting five.

stories.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Heat host Tyler Herro, Bucks for GTA 6-inspired 'Vice City' night
stories.summary: Wednesday's game will also be the first time that Antetokounmpo has faced the Bucks since his trade to the Heat last offseason.
stories.detailText: The Miami Heat are playing host to the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday night. While this was already a big game — the first time Giannis Antetokounmpo is facing his former team — it carries even more meaning. The long-awaited "GTA VI" releases nationwide on Thursday. It is arguably the most highly anticipated video game of all time, coming out 13 years after GTA V was released back in 2013. The game, which has already received near-perfect reviews , is set to upend the world Thursda. With estimates that roughly 16 million copies of the game were pre-ordered, employers could be dealing with a lot of "sick" days ahead of the weekend. That might sound far-fetched, but it's true. Experts are estimating businesses in the United States could lose over $1 billion in productivity due to worker absences . "Vice City" is a fictional city from the franchise. It is not a direct replica of Miami, but it is heavily inspired by the city, while the state of "Leonida" in the video game is inspired by Florida. The Heat's marketing department took the chance to host a "Vice City"-inspired night in honor of the game's release, and it just so happened to coincide with Anteokounmpo getting his first crack at his old team. To celebrate the game's release, the Kaseya Center got a "Vice City" makeover with a new paint job. Music from the video game was also played throughout the arena. Antetokounmpo has already made an impact with his new team. Heading into Wednesday's game, he has played in 14 games this year and is averaging 28.3 points, 12.5 rebounds, and 5.2 assists per game. stories.title: NBA Europe appears headed for 'soft launch' next fall
stories.summary: It's less than a year until Adam Silver said he hoped to launch NBA Europe and no formal deals are in place.
stories.detailText: Jun 23, 2026; New York, NY, USA; NBA commissioner Adam Silver speaks during the 2026 NBA Draft at Barclays Center. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Commissioner Adam Silver has said he wants NBA Europe to launch in the fall of 2027 — and it appears he is going to get his wish. Sort of. Just not in the way he or others may have originally envisioned. There are only 11 months between now and Silver's proposed launch date, and NBA Europe has yet to have any formal agreements with teams. Negotiations with the EuroLeague — some of the teams the NBA is eyeing are members of it — have slowed. That could lead to a "soft launch" of the league next fall, reports The Athletic’s Joe Vardon . A member of one of the ownership groups of a potential NBA Europe club put it this way to Vardon: "Broadly speaking, it is implausible that a serious league could be launched (by next October)." The idea of a "soft launch" has been floated before and is not something the NBA has pushed back on — this was always a possibility. Building something sustainable long term was always going to take time and the league understood that. The NBA is partnering with FIBA (the international basketball organization that puts on the World Cup and helps pick teams for the Olympics) on an NBA Europe plan that calls for 12 permanent teams and four open spots teams could play their way into through domestic leagues and tournaments. Those dozen permanent teams would be made up of some existing European powerhouses — FC Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, and Panathinaikos of Greece have been mentioned, among others — plus teams in major European markets such as Rome, Paris, Lyon and others (some of those teams could be tied to existing soccer powers, but not all). What would make things smoother is an agreement or merger with the EuroLeague — the continent's existing preeminent basketball competition — but a couple of months ago EuroLeague shareholders rejected the NBA's initial proposal. The challenge is that EuroLeague has 13 permanent members and only some of them would be jumping to NBA Europe, which is a bit messy. That said, the sides are still talking, and it's possible they reach some kind of arrangement. What would a "soft launch" look like? From The Athletic: So, a soft launch could, in theory, include a qualifying tournament in the fall of 2027. Another possibility for NBA Europe's 2027 version is if, as expected, the NBA formalizes agreements with at least some existing European teams to join as NBA Europe licensed franchises over the next few months. Those teams could play each other in some precursory competition that ultimately becomes NBA Europe. NBA owners are fully backing Silver and the NBA Europe plan because it's essentially free money for them. Silver and the NBA have met with potential teams and investors and expect franchise fees in the $500 million to $1 billion range for each of the 12 permanent members. What the NBA wants is to modernize – and better monetize — the basketball infrastructure in Europe. As part of its plan, the league is looking at a multibillion-dollar infrastructure fund to pay for arena construction, including for existing teams (which may already have arenas), bringing more modern NBA-style arenas to those cities.

stories.title: The missing Gen-Z reaction that told JJ Redick this Lakers team was special
stories.summary: Lakers' chemistry is off the charts.
stories.detailText: Long before the Lakers were the best story in the NBA , JJ Redick had an inkling that this team was different. It clicked for him after the Lakers had a team dinner at Carbone Riviera in Las Vegas in July. After general manager Rob Pelinka paid the bill, Redick became hyperaware of what had not happened that evening. “I get up to leave and it struck me,” he said. “Nobody had left. Nobody had been on their phone.” Those may seem like small things. But they were indicative of the character of the group. The players wanted to bond. They wanted to be around one another. Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic reacts to a charging foul during a game against the Charlotte Hornets, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, in Los Angeles. Getty Images They were in Sin City, surrounded by a million distractions, but they chose to spend their time with one another. Now a team that was expected to be a mile behind the Thunder and Spurs in the Western Conference has the best record in the league at 13-2. They’ve won nine games in a row. They’ve announced themselves as real championship contenders . The Lakers have surpassed expectations. They’re leading the league in offensive rating (123.1) and steals (10.8) and they’re third in blocks (6.1). Their chemistry is palpable. Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick calls out directions against the Portland Trail Blazers in Los Angeles on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. Getty Images Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves constantly tease each other as though they were brothers. Their affinity for one another has spilled onto the court, where they’re the top-scoring duo in the league, averaging a combined 63.5 points per game. Walker Kessler has a contagious positivity. He’s also a beast down low and a double-double machine, averaging 14.5 points and 10.9 rebounds per game. And the Lakers’ role players are starring in their roles. That was never more obvious than in the Lakers’ 118-114 overtime win over the Hornets on Tuesday. The Lakers were without Kessler (right lower leg soreness) and Reaves (left heel bruise). Doncic was in foul trouble. The Lakers trailed by as much as 18 points. But they refused to drop the rope. Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic, left, slaps hands with head coach JJ Redick during an NBA game Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, in Los Angeles. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill Doncic realized Quentin Grimes had a hot hand . He started waving off Redick’s play calls in the fourth quarter, so he could feed his teammate. Grimes went on to finish with a career-high 47 points, becoming the only Laker to score 10 or more 3-pointers in a game other than Kobe Bryant in the Lakers’ win. Things have just come together for the Lakers. There’s a good feeling in the locker room. The guys genuinely like each other. And that’s dangerous for the rest of the league. “I think at the end of the day we have great chemistry, which is in my opinion very important,” Doncic said. “But I think this group is very special.” It’s interesting because the Lakers weren’t supposed to jell this quickly. Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick looks on against the Atlanta Hawks during the fourth quarter at State Farm Arena in Atlanta on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. Getty Images They have nine new players. Doncic has never been known as a vocal leader. This was supposed to be a transition year after LeBron James left in free agency and the Lakers overhauled their roster around the Slovenian superstar. But something happened over the summer that changed things. A seed was planted in Vegas. And it flourished after Doncic flew his teammates to Slovenia to host a mini camp, something he had never done before in his career. They laughed. They sightsaw. They bonded with each other and grew a much deeper understanding of their biggest star. It’s paying off. Redick believes what’s happening right now is a magical coalescence of opportunity meeting the right personnel. It has resulted in a locker room with good vibes. A team that’s soaring. And a coach who is deeply grateful that his gut feeling was correct. He first saw it months ago, long before they ever stepped foot on the court. “I don’t know what this is going to look like after 82 games,” Redick said. “I don’t know what it’s going to look like after 50. But I do know that there’s something with this group. Every special group doesn’t mean you win a championship. “But it’s a special group of guys.”

stories.detailText: DENVER, COLORADO - FEBRUARY 25: Payton Pritchard #11 of the Boston Celtics dribbles against Nikola Jokic #15 of the Denver Nuggets in the first half at Ball Arena on February 25, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. This is the first of 2 games between these two teams this season. They will face off again in Boston on February 9. The Celtics were 0-2 last season against the Nuggets. They are 62-42 overall, all time, against the Nuggets and they are 21-31 in games played in Denver. With their loss to the Magic, the Celtics have dropped to 2nd in the East, half a game behind the first place 76ers. They are 2 games ahead of 3rd place Detroit. They are 2-3 at home and 4-2 on the road. They are 6-4 in their last 10 games and they are 2-0 against Eastern Conference opponents. They are coming off a loss in their last game. The Nuggets have made a few changes since last season but no major changes. They have added free agents Marvin Bagley III, Alpha Diallo, and Tyus Jones. They then play one game at home against Atlanta before playing at San Antonio and Dallas. Then it’s home against Charlotte before a game at Brooklyn. Next they have a 7 game home stand against Washington twice, Utah, Detroit, Portland, Miami and Cleveland. I’m going to guess that the Celtics will be starting their regular starting lineup of Derrick White, Jordan Walsh, Paul George, Jayson Tatum and Neemias Queta. Of course, Joe can always surprise us with an unexpected change at any time. I’m going with the Denver starting line up of Jamal Murray, Christian Braun, Cam Johnson, Aaron Gordon and Nikola Vucevic from their Game Notes. The Celtics have no one on their injury report at this time. Since they aren’t playing back to back games, they should not have to rest anyone. The Nuggets have just Julian Strawther on their injury report. He was was diagnosed with a left knee sprain in a preseason game and has yet to make his debut in the regular season. He is averaging 24.1 points, 10.9 rebounds, 8.9 assists, 1.1 blocks and 1.8 steals per game. He is shooting 51.6% from the field and 26.0% from beyond the arc. Over his career, against the Celtics, he has averaged 23.1 points, 10.8 rebounds 6.9 assists and 1.2 steals per game. He is a handful and the Celtics need to try to slow him down by any means necessary and especially keep him out of the paint. Derrick White vs Jamal Murray Murray is averaging 26.1 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 6.0 assists per game. He is shooting 53.5% from the field and 47.1% from beyond the arc. Over his career against the Celtics, he has averaged 19.8 points, 4.9 rebounds, 5.3 assists and 1.1 steals. The Celtics will need to defend Murray very well both on the perimeter and in the paint as he can put up points in a hurry. Honorable Mention Jordan Walsh vs Christian Braun Braun is averaging 12.6 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 2.3 assists and 2.2 steals per game. He is shooting 48.3% from the field and 35.2% from beyond the arc. Over his career against the Celtics, he has averaged 7.3 points, 4.0 rebounds, and 1.5 assist per game. Keys to the Game Defense – Defense is the key to winning every game. The Celtics are 2nd with a defensive rating of 106.1. The Nuggets have a defensive rating of 114.9, which is 20th. The Celtics are 5th in the league with an offensive rating of 118.2 and the Nuggets are 10th with an offensive rating of 115.1. The Celtics have made defense their identity but against the Magic, their effort on that end was lacking. They need to go all out every game on the defensive end to win this and every game. Rebound – Rebounding is another key to winning every game. The Celtics are 10th in the league, averaging 44.9 rebounds per game. The Nuggets are 25th in the league with 41.7 rebounds per game. Rebounding takes effort and the Celtics have to work harder to grab rebounds to limit the Nuggets second chance points and fast breaks. The Celtics are 7-1 when they have more rebounds than their opponents. They have to put in the effort to beat the Nuggets on the boards. Effort and Energy for 48 Minutes – The Celtics must be the more aggressive team. They have to fight for loose balls, defend aggressively, be aggressive in driving to the basket, and just play harder than the Nuggets for the entire game. They have to be the team that wants it more and plays like it. They especially have to begin the game with energy and not allow the Nuggets to race out to a big lead and then, they can’t let up throughout the game. They also have to come out strong in the 3rd quarter and play hard until the final buzzer. They allowed the Magic to play harder than them, especially in the 4th quarter and they can’t do that in this game if they want to win it. Move the Ball Carefully – The Celtics need to keep moving the ball to find the open man. Doing that makes it much harder to guard them. However, they have to be careful with their passes and they also need to be careful when they dribble the ball and not drive into a crowd and turn the ball over. The Celtics are usually very good at taking care of the ball but at times they lose focus and get sloppy. They can’t afford to do that against the Nuggets. X-Factors Mile High on the Road – It’s tough to win in Denver because of the altitude that the teams are playing at. Denver is called the Mile High City because it is 5,280 feet above sea level. Nuggets players are used to the altitude but visiting teams often struggle with playing there and often are fatigued before the end of the game. It is a very unique home court advantage. The Celtics also have to shake off the distractions of travel and playing in front of a hostile crowd and play hard and play their game. Officiating – I know that I say this every game, but the officiating can always be an x-factor. Every crew calls the game differently whether they call every little ticky tack foul or they let a lot of contact go and let the teams play. We have already seen games where the officiating made a difference in the outcome, both good and bad. The Celtics have got to adjust to the way the game is being called and not let the calls affect their focus or their play. The Celtics also have to be aware of the new points of emphasis for this season and try to avoid flopping, off‑arm push‑offs, reckless closeouts, delays before free throws, and illegal screens.

stories.detailText: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 12: Jose Alvarado #5 of the New York Knicks in action during the third quarter of a preseason game against the Minnesota Timberwolves at Madison Square Garden on October 12, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following Thursday’s drunken back-and-forth beautiful mess of a come-from-behind win , it’s time for Karl-Anthony Towns and the NBA Champion New York Knicks to come to town for their first matchup of the season. Despite winning seven of their last eight games, this will be the Wolves’ third game in four nights after having a very physical back-to-back against the Portland Trail Blazers. Meanwhile, the Knicks have won six of their last eight games and will now travel to Minnesota at the vert tail end of a four-game road trip. They most recently played Tuesday night in Toronto where they took care of a Kawhi Leonard-less Raptors team in the clutch. It is Karl-Anthony Towns that deserves first billing in this matchup. In his previous two visits to Target Center since the trade, KAT is averaging 36 points, 16.5 rebounds, 3.5 assists, and is a +37 in all his minutes in the opposing team’s uniform in Minneapolis. At an 8-6 overall record, don’t let the Knicks middling record fool you into thinking this team is just cruising through the regular season with a championship hangover. Since their 0-3 start, the Knicks are 8-3 with all of their losses in that time coming within single digits. In those 11 games, they are the third ranked team in net rating, trailing just the San Antonio Spurs and Boston Celtics . They are traveling to Minneapolis with a fully healthy squad and will be looking to stack more wins to climb out of the mire of the middle of the Eastern Conference. Game Info Who : Minnesota Timberwolves (11-4) vs New York Knicks (8-6) When : 7:00pm CST Where : Target Center, Minneapolis Minnesota Local TV : DAZN-MIN | NBA TV Radio : 830 WCCO Ratings and Key Stats Wolves Offensive Rating : 12th Defensive Rating : 1st Net Rating : 3rd Team EPM Rank : 8th Key Strength Stat : Points in the paint (5th) Key Weakness Stat : Assist Percentage (28th) Spider-Man Pointing Meme Stat : Second Chance Points (3rd) Knicks Offensive Rating : 10th Defensive Rating : 6th Net Rating : 8th Team EPM Rank : 5th Key Strength Stat : Offensive Rebounding Percentage (1st) Key Weakness Stat : Pace (30th) Spider-Man Pointing Meme Stat : Second Chance Points (1st) View Link What To Watch For: Who controls the paint? Over the last ten games, the Wolves are second in the league in points in the paint thanks in large part to Ayo Dosunmo’s increased usage and desire to win a footrace to the rim each time he catches the ball. The Knicks are the third best team at defending the paint thanks to a core of very versatile wing defenders who are able to switch on everything and stay in prime position defensively. Couple their paint defense with being the best rebounding team in the league and it is clear where their money is made on the defensive end. They want to force you to hit shots from midrange and beyond, and then grab rebounds with their long and athletic wings. The Wolves are no slouches themselves with the sixth best rebounding percentage. They utilize a very similar front court when they are fully healthy. The Knicks play at the slowest pace in the league and utilize a half-court offense that is going to feature a lot of Jalen Brunson trying to get to the rim and draw (or at least make it look like he’s drawn) contact. The Wolves defend well without fouling (5th best opponent free throw rate), but the NBA Finals MVP always has a few tricks up his sleeve that could get Wolves defenders in foul trouble. If things are mucked up in the paint like the above numbers suggest, the importance of the Wolves making the “one extra pass” to an open shooter and converting could well be the secret sauce to unlocking offense against a very versatile defensive team. Isolation basketball that leans too heavily into the Wolves’ 28th ranked assisting percentage will absolutely make this game feel like the Wolves are pushing a boulder uphill all night long. The X-Factor : The Health of Jonathan Kuminga The Knicks starting group of Jalen Brunson, Mikal Bridges, Josh Hart, OG Anunoby and KAT is a rare starting group that is as versatile as the Wolves. If Kuminga can’t go and Minnesota chooses to put Jaden McDaniels on Jalen Brunson, there are going to be a lot of matchup issues for the Wolves. Assuming LaMelo Ball takes Josh Hart, Dosunmo will shift to Bridges, leaving OG Anunoby with a tantalizing matchup with either a size advantage on Cody Williams, or a speed and athleticism advantage on Trey “Elite Rim Protector” Lyles. While Dosunmo could be on Brunson duty instead McDaniels, the defensive scheme makes a whole lot more sense if Kuminga is good to go. Prediction My prediction is all based on the X-Factor of Jonathan Kuminga’s availability Thursday. If he plays, the Wolves win a physical back-and-forth defensive slug fest 106-102 where Kuminga can match physicality with OG Anunoby. If he’s out, the Wolves just won’t have quite enough bodies to throw at the trio of Brunson, Bridges, and Anunoby, losing 116-106. Wait for Kuminga’s game status to be announced then go place your bets as the outcome has already been foretold!

stories.title: How LeBron James' move from Lakers to 76ers unlocked both teams' superpowers
stories.summary: The Lakers are thriving without LeBron James, the 76ers are thriving with James and two former NBA general managers help make sense of it all.
stories.detailText: The NBA standings , heading into games scheduled for Wednesday, Nov. 18, tell a remarkable story involving LeBron James. The Los Angeles Lakers , the team James left before the 2026-27 season, are 13-2 and off to their best start since 2008-09 (14-1 to start that season). That season, the Lakers won the NBA title. The Philadelphia 76ers , the team James joined before this season, are 12-3 and off to their best start since 2000-01. That season, the 76ers reached the NBA Finals and lost to…the Lakers. “You never know what… change can totally affect your team,’’ said Randy Pfund, part of the Lakers coaching staff from 1985 to 1994 and general manager of the Miami Heat from 1995 to 2008. Of course the oddity here is, four weeks into the season, the team James left and the team he joined both appear to have gotten better. Why the Lakers are thriving without LeBron James Analytics can help explain how the Lakers are thriving without James. Especially as presented by Vangelis Sarlis, a Greek postdoctoral researcher who has mined NBA data. “I would describe it as role redistribution rather than addition by subtraction,’’ Vangelis Sarlis told USA TODAY Sports. “…The more persuasive analytical explanation is that LeBron’s departure clarified roles.'' With James no longer playing for the Lakers, Luka Dončić leads the league in scoring with 38.8 points per game and twice has scored more than 50 points. “Luka Dončić is now the unquestioned primary creator and Austin Reaves the secondary creator, with personnel around them designed for spacing, screening and finishing,'' said Sarlis, whose research team includes George Papageorgiou and professor Christos Tjortjis at International Hellenic University in Thermi, Greece. Their work includes the 2024 academic paper titled "Leveraging Sports Analytics and Association Rule Mining to Uncover Recovery and Economic Impacts in NBA Basketball." Through 14 games, Sarlis pointed out that the Lakers’ offensive rating had risen from 118.2 last season to about 123 points per 100 possessions, the best in the league. He also cited NBA tracking that shows the Lakers have experienced the league’s biggest jump in transition scoring, from 22.6 to 26.2 points per game. “That supports the observation that the offense looks quicker and more fluid,’’ Sarlis said. He also noted Dončić’s usage rate of 40.2%, which leads the league in adding to the Lakers’ offense: “It's faster, but it is more concentrated, not less.’’ Then there was James’ $52 million salary with the Lakers. The funds once spent on him allowed the Lakers to re-sign Reeves and overhaul the roster. Key additions include center Walker Kessler, who’s averaging 14.5 points per game and 10.9 rebounds per game; guard Quentin Grimes, who is averaging 12.1 points per game and scored 47 points in the Lakers’ 118-114 overtime victory against the Charlotte Hornets Tuesday, Nov. 17; and Sandro Mamukelashvili and Collin Sexton, both notable contributors. “That personnel is…the most concrete link to LeBron’s departure,’’ Sarlis said. How LeBron James fits with the 76ers LeBron James is not the same player who won four NBA titles, including one with the Lakers during the COVID-shortened season in 2020. In 11 games played this season, James' shooting percentage (.443) is the worst since his rookie year and his 3-point shooting percentage (.225) is the worst of his career. But Bob Whitsitt, former general manager of the Seattle Supersonics and Portland Trail Blazers, suggested the early-season shooting trouble obscures James’ contributions. “He's always been a good passer, but maybe right now his passing is a little bit more of what's needed in Philly than the other things he's doing,’’ Whitsitt said. James leads the 76ers with 6.9 assists per game. No one seems to be overly concerned he's averaging only 15.1 points on a team with potent scorers like Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid. “Rather than expecting LeBron to remain the primary scorer, the 76ers can utilize him as a fourth scoring option, playmaker and facilitator alongside Embiid, Maxey, and Brown,’’ said Sarlis, the Greek researcher. “His experience and basketball intelligence could help optimize team rotations and strengthen Philadelphia's pursuit of another championship.’’ Why veteran experience could matter in the playoffs Pfund won two NBA championship rings as a member of the Lakers’ coaching staff from 1985 to 1994. He won a third NBA championship ring as the general manager of the Miami Heat from 1995 to 2008. He also spent most of his NBA career working for legendary Pat Riley. “Pat always believed you could never have too many veteran guys who would come through in the clutch,’’ Pfund said. Sarlis said his team's research shows James, 41, is among the most consistent historical performers in decisive moment. Clutch veterans are most valuable in the playoffs, said Pfund, who cited two examples. In February 1987, when Pfund was an assistant on the Lakers’ coaching staff, Lakers traded for center Mychal Thompson. He was was an 8th-year NBA veteran. Not only did he prove to be a capable backup center behind Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, he also played a role in the Lakers’ winning the 1987 NBA title. “Mychal Thompson was huge,’’ Pfund said. Then in 2005, when Pfund was the general manager of the Heat, the team at Riley's behest traded for Antoine Walker. He was an 11 th year veteran and three-time All Star with the Boston Celtics. “He was pretty average all year,’’ Pfund said. “And people were (saying), man, they spent too much money and whatever.’’ But the veteran player delivered in the postseason., according Pfund. “Antoine Walker had made a lot of big baskets,’’ Pfund said. “He didn't hesitate at all.’’ The Heat beat the Dallas Mavericks in the 2006 NBA title, winning the franchise's first NBA title. What's next It's still five weeks away from the NBA's slate of Christmas Day games, which this year will include -- you guessed it -- the 76ers vs. the Lakers at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. But Whitsitt, the former NBA general manager, allowed himself to think well beyond Christmas. "What kind of story would it be if the Lakers played the Sixers in the Finals?'' he said. It's an enticing possibility as Whitsitt talked about what he expects to happen next. James will continue to blend in with his new teammates. The Lakers will eventually tighten up on defense. Hopefully, both teams will stay healthy as the season unfolds. "They're both fun to watch,'' Whitsitt said. stories.title: Media firebrand asks if Black players will let Lakers’ ‘white brothers’ win it all
stories.summary: Stephen A. Smith had a question for Black NBA players on Wednesday morning after the Lakers won their ninth straight game. “These white brothers can play, they can play. They...
stories.detailText: Stephen A. Smith had a question for Black NBA players on Wednesday morning after the Lakers won their ninth straight game. “These white brothers can play, they can play. They can win a championship. This is the NBA!” Smith said on “First Take.” “Y’all gonna let them win a championship?” Los Angeles Lakers forward Ziaire Williams, Luka Doncic, Jake LaRavia and Walker Kessler wait during a time-out in Phoenix, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. AP Photo/Darryl Webb Smith was talking about a Lakers team built around Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler. A week earlier, he had picked Los Angeles to bow out by the second round, saying on Mad Dog Sports Radio that he had never seen a team win a title with three white players as its best players. Stephen A. wonders if Black players around the league are going to let the Lakers win a championship "I'm looking at the brothers, and I'm saying, LA doing special things…these white brothers can play, y'all gonna let them win a championship?" pic.twitter.com/2ZNKcUW1H1 — NBACentral (@TheDunkCentral) November 18, 2026 He still doubts the Lakers will win it all, but he and fellow ESPN analyst Chiney Ogwumike agree they can. Smith framed the question around race. Ogwumike made the stronger case for the Lakers by pointing to what Doncic did with the game on the line . He trusted Quentin Grimes to take the biggest shot of the night. Luka Doncic reacts to making a bad pass during the second half against the Charlotte Hornets in Los Angeles, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. Getty Images But Smith made the question about race. Ogwumike pointed to something that says more about the Lakers’ title chances. With the game on the line, Luka Doncic trusted Quentin Grimes to take the biggest shot of the night. The final possession of regulation in Tuesday’s 118-114 overtime win over Charlotte gave her a reason to believe. With Reaves and Kessler sidelined, the Lakers had rallied from 18 down and needed a 3 to stay alive. Doncic had 36 points and a single defender in front of him. Grimes had his hands up. Quentin Grimes of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts after scoring during a game against the Charlotte Hornets in Los Angeles, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. Getty Images Doncic found him. Grimes buried the tying 3 with 1.7 seconds left. It was his 10th of the night, making him and Kobe Bryant the only Lakers to hit that many in a game. Grimes finished with a career-high 47. “It’s the vibe. It’s the ability to say, ‘Hey, we have enough to pursue a championship,’” Ogwumike said on ESPN. “Not gonna lie, when I heard that, I was like, I’m not sure about that.” Where Smith raised the question of race, Ogwumike saw what could make the Lakers champions: chemistry developing between the Lakers’ best player and a new addition attempting to make his mark. “That doesn’t start in that moment,” she said. “That starts in training camp.”

stories.title: JJ Redick revealed the Lakers’ strategy with two-way signings this season
stories.summary: Los Angeles wants players who fit into valuable NBA roles, not necessarily the G League’s best players

NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tuesday night, with Walker Kessler sidelined and his replacement, Kevon Looney, struggling, the Los Angeles Lakers turned to Carson Cooper for minutes at center. Signed to a two-way contract on Nov. 10, Cooper gave the Lakers 18 minutes and logged three points (0-of-1 shooting, 3-of-6 at the line), four rebounds (two offensive) and two assists. Los Angeles outscored the Charlotte Hornets by six points during his time on the floor. After Cooper’s Lakers debut, head coach JJ Redick spoke about what the organization is prioritizing with its two-way contract players, whether it’s Cooper, Chris Mañon, Arthur Kaluma or AK Okereke (who was waived last month and is now playing for the Coachella Valley Lakers). The goal, Redick said, isn’t to simply land the foremost G League stars but to find those who can fill valuable roles for the Lakers when called upon, just as Cooper did Tuesday. “I think [Carson Cooper] understands the assignment. Not to get too big picture with what the G League is and what the two-ways are, but I think philosophically, we’ve gone in a bunch of different directions with our two-ways and I think with this group, like we really wanted to get guys that could play a role for this team if needed,” Redick told reporters following the 118-114 win . “With Chris and with both the AKs…and Carson’s the same way. He’s here to play a role and it’s not, ‘Oh, this guy can go score 30 points in the G League.’ That doesn’t necessarily equate to what we need right now. And so all our guys that are two-ways this year, they understand why they’re in that role and how they can impact winning and help our team and he did that tonight for us.” Kessler isn’t listed on Wednesday’s injury report, so the Lakers will welcome back their preferred choice at center against the Utah Jazz . But given Looney’s struggles to open the year and the general lack of reliable options behind Kessler, it’s absolutely possible Cooper receives some more run down the line this season. At the very least, it sounds like Tuesday was a nice audition in his head coach’s eyes. You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

stories.title: The longest single-opponent winning streaks in Knicks history
stories.summary: Two Atlantic Division foes haven’t been the Knicks in four years. Think about that.
stories.detailText: TORONTO, CANADA - NOVEMBER 17: Karl-Anthony Towns #32 of the New York Knicks smiles after the game against the Toronto Raptors on November 17, 2026 at the Scotiabank Arena in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Mark Blinch/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images On Tuesday night, the Knicks outlasted the Raptors for the second time in three nights to extend a staggering 15-game winning streak against their Canadian rivals that dates back to January 2023. Beyond the fact that it means that old friends RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley have never beaten their old team, it also extends one of the longest streaks in program history against a single opponent. Celtics, 21 games (1993-98) As mentioned on last night’s broadcast, it’s hard to believe such a dominant stretch existed against a longtime rival that has been the Eastern Conference’s banner of success for generations. Simply, the sport is cyclical, and the few times the Celtics were in the doldrums, the Knicks were contending for titles. Through the many dark ages of Knicks history, the Celtics dominated. It’s why they’ve only faced off in the postseason three times in the last 35 years. From 1965-67, the Celtics won 21 in a row against the Knicks in the heart of the Bill Russell era. It took 25 years to return the favor. On January 10, 1993, the Celtics outlasted the Knicks at TD Garden in a 100-97 win. They wouldn’t win another game in this rivalry for over five years. The Celtics won 48 games in 1992-93, but quickly fell into the East’s cellar. They wouldn’t win 40 games again in a season until 2001-02, while at the same time, Patrick Ewing and the Knicks had only the Bulls and Pacers competing with them for spots in the NBA Finals yearly. Ewing would score 65 combined over the next two meetings in April 1993 before scoring 30 again on Opening Night that October in a three-point win in Boston. He routinely owned the Celtics during this time, reaching a crescendo with a 36-14 effort in March 1994. November 5, 1993: New York’s Anthony Mason scores on a circus shot in Boston. Mason scored 18 PTS off the bench and Patrick Ewing scored a game-high 32 PTS in the Knicks’ 111-108 win. Robert Parish finished with 20 PTS for the Celtics. pic.twitter.com/tehTtw4Dmd — NBA Cobwebs (@NBACobwebs) November 5, 2026 As the Celtics got worse, the Knicks took advantage of them more and more. A 35-point blowout in February 1994 still stands as one of the biggest blowouts in the rivalry’s history. Hubert Davis nailed five threes and scored 25 points in a 90-83 win the following month. It was always a different enemy that flummoxed the Celtics. Charles Smith scoring 25, Anthony Mason scoring 21, and John Starks and Ewing’s consistency. Even as Pat Riley turned into Jeff Van Gundy, the Knicks never lost a step. The streak had reached 17 by January 28, 1997, when the pitiful 9-30 Celtics put the greatest scare into the contending Knicks yet. An eight-point lead in the final minutes dwindled to a tie on a Todd Day three in the final minute before free throws by Antoine Walker gave Boston the lead in the final minute. Just when the streak appeared over, Chris Childs called game with eight seconds left. Eventually, the streak would finally end on January 26, 1998, when the Knicks were held to just 85 points behind a 25-point gem by Chauncey Billups. Even this triumphant victory came with an asterisk, as Ewing missed the game due to wrist surgery. Huh. Cavaliers, 18 games (1980-83) The Knicks own the Cavs in the playoffs, but did you know there was a stretch they owned them like this? In five all-time playoff meetings, the Knicks are 16-2 against the Cavs, but once took things to another level in the early 1980s. Unlike the Celtics, this is pretty peculiar. The Knicks were an average team during this streak, but took advantage of one of the worst eras of Cavs basketball under Ted Stepien. Quite precisely, this streak can be known as the “Stepien Streak”, as while he was owner from April 1980 to his sale in April 1983, the Cavs went 1-16 against the Knicks, with the lone win coming just two weeks before he sold the team in late March of 1983. Highlights of the streak include Mike Glenn’s 29-point game in November 1980 (second-highest scoring game of his career), Ray Williams’ 37-point gem in an overtime win two weeks later, and perennially playing in front of 4,000 fans at an empty Richfield Coliseum. The NBA was totally different in the 80s. Bullets, 17 games (1952-53) Back in the day, there weren’t many teams. As such, you get stuff like this. Over a span of 400 days from February 6, 1952, to March 11, 1953, the Knicks played the Baltimore Bullets 17 times and won every single one of them. The 1950s Knicks can sometimes be referred to as the Silver Era of Knicks basketball due to the team making multiple Finals appearances before Russell came and made the East his own, so it’s no surprise they were dominant. But like this? The lore of 1950s NBA is quite fascinating. These teams played each other three times in six days in February 1952 when the streak began, but played the games in three different places. The Bullets won 82-81 in the Baltimore Coliseum on February 4, the Knicks won 73-70 at the 69th Regiment Armory on February 6, and the two teams met in Philadelphia on February 8 in a 20-point blowout win for Ray Lumpp and the Knicks. On March 5, the teams participated in a doubleheader at the Boston Garden, preceding a game between the Bucks and Celtics later that night. In 1952-53, when the Knicks went 10-0 against the Bullets en route to a Finals appearance, they played one game in Philly, two games in Boston (one of which went to triple overtime), and even played in Trenton, New Jersey, on March 5, 1953. Finally, the Bullets snapped the skid on November 14, 1953, behind 19 points by Max Zaslofsky in Baltimore. Just for the hell of it, here’s some other weird neutral site locations from the 1950s: January 29, 1952, in Louisville (vs. Indianapolis Olympians) February 3, 1953, in Buffalo (vs. Milwaukee Hawks) February 18, 1953, in Providence (vs. Boston Celtics) January 22, 1954, in New Haven, CT (vs. Philadelphia Warriors) Several times in 1954-55 in Miami (vs. Fort Wayne Pistons) November 18, 1954, in Syracuse (vs. Philadelphia Warriors) March 3, 1955, in Saratoga Springs (vs. Milwaukee Hawks) March 13, 1956, in Moorhead, MN (vs. Minneapolis Lakers) January 17, 1957, in Lacrosse, WI (vs. Minneapolis Lakers) January 14, 1958, in St. Louis (vs. Cincinnati Royals) February 21, 1958, in Camden, NJ (vs. Philadelphia Warriors) January 22, 1962, in Moline, IL (vs. Chicago Packers) March 12, 1962, in Seattle (vs. Los Angeles Lakers) Various times in Hershey, PA (including the Wilt 100 game) Pistons, 16 games (2020-24) We’ve seen a new standard of excellence for the Knicks since the turn of the decade, They have three of these streaks in the last six years! Back when the Pistons weren’t the annoying playoff contenders we know them as now, they were pretty damn awful. For years, it was a running joke that the COVID-19 pandemic was younger than the last Pistons win over the Knicks. The streak began on February 8, 2020, when the Knicks overcame an early double-digit deficit to outlast the Pistons in Detroit in a battle of two lowly teams that wouldn’t even be invited to the bubble. Another win on March 8 would mark the team’s final home game with fans for another year due to the pandemic. As the Knicks ascended, the Pistons stayed bad. On April 4, 2021, the Knicks eviscerated them by a 125-81 margin, the second-biggest blowout in the over 430 games in this matchup. Even as the meltdown in 2021-22 ensued, the orange and blue survived a scare that March when Marvin Bagley III dropped 27, only for Alec Burks to strip Cade Cunningham in the final seconds to hold on. The most memorable game of the streak came at the end. Facing the 8-48 Pistons at home in late February, the Knicks came out sleepy and watched as Cunningham nearly dragged his hapless team to the finish line to end the skid at 14, but shenanigans ensued with Donte DiVincenzo to somehow pull it off with a Josh Hart and-1. Was it a foul? Does anyone really care? The streak ended on December 7, 2024. We didn’t know it at the time, but the Pistons had finally emerged as threats, and they’d start their own six-game regular-season winning streak against the Knicks that lasted until three weeks ago. Raptors and Nets, 15 games (active) The last time the Raptors beat the Knicks? January 22, 2023. The last time the Nets beat the Knicks? January 28, 2023. The next opportunity for both to beat the Knicks? Brooklyn gets another chance on December 27, while Toronto next gets a crack on January 20. It’ll be basically four years for both since their last win. These two streaks are tied for the fourth-longest active streaks in the NBA. The three longer? OKC over Memphis, Cleveland over Washington, and the Clippers over the Hornets, all at 17. If you thought four years was a lot, it’s been almost 10 since the Hornets beat the Clippers! These two streaks are very different, but also the same. Both teams have been worse than the Knicks this entire time, sometimes considerably worse, and have yielded some ugly blowouts. There have also been plenty of scares. There’s the Brunson game-winner in the NBA Cup, the KAT heroics in The Six, the times that Brooklyn puts up a fight but folds late at Barclays Center, and the multiple double-digit comebacks we saw this week. Either way, those are two Atlantic Division rivals that can’t beat the Knicks. It also comes directly after both dominated the Knicks for prolonged periods. Remember Nic Claxton’s comments? Well, at the time, the Knicks were 0-9 against the Nets from 2020-23. The Raptors went a blistering 23-5 against the Knicks from January 2016 to November 2023. Ain’t no fun when the rabbit’s got the gun.

stories.title: Game Preview: Phoenix Suns continue road trip against Sacramento Kings
stories.summary: The Phoenix Suns face a team with no life. Will the starters take another step against a subpar Kings team?
stories.detailText: Who : Phoenix Suns (6-7) vs. Sacramento Kings (1-12) When : 8:00 pm Arizona Time Where : Golden 1 Center — Sacramento, California Watch : Arizona’s Family 3TV, Arizona’s Family Sports, NBATV Listen : KMVP 98.7 The Phoenix Suns roll into Sacramento with five wins in their last seven games, while Sacramento comes in on a six-game losing streak. For the Suns, this game is all about building off of their best performance of the season against the Denver Nuggets Monday night. In that game, the Suns’ 4 main starters all scored above 15 points, which is just the second time they have done that this season. Even more importantly, the second-half energy and defensive intensity were the best minutes they have played together. Dillon Brooks and Jalen Green both looked as confident and aggressive as they have all season, without disrupting the flow of everyone else on the floor. Jordan Ott made some rotation adjustments against Denver that worked well, and against a Kings team that is the bottom of the barrel in the NBA, look for him to tinker with lineups even more. Do we see more Koa Peat after he only played one minute against the Nuggets? The Suns can start this five-game road swing 2-0 and take another positive step in establishing the team identity for the rest of the season, regardless of whether it is the starter or bench units on the floor. Tale of the Tape Probable Starters Injury Report Suns Mark Williams — OUT (Shoulder Surgery) Kings Precious Achiuwa — QUESTIONABLE (Lower Leg Contusion) De’Andre Hunter — QUESTIONABLE (Left Hip Soreness) Maxime Raynaud — OUT (Right Patella Subluxation) Ben Simmons — OUT (Right Achilles Tendon) What to Watch For The Phoenix Suns are going up against a rookie point guard in Darius Acuff Jr., who loves to shoot and is averaging over four turnovers per game. He is the head of the snake, and the Suns’ commitment to not letting him get going and forcing him into difficult situations to create easy opportunities going the other way is what I will be watching for defensively. These are the two worst rebounding teams in the NBA, so it is an opportunity for the Suns to show they are a steadily improving rebounding team against a team that does not rebound well. When the Suns defend and rebound with energy, it unlocks the version of this team that can be better than last year’s team because it is healthier and more talented. Do we see that against the Kings, or do the Suns try to sleepwalk against the Kings squad that has not played well this season? If the Suns starters do try and sleepwalk their way through this game, the bench is more than capable of picking up the slack. The Kings bench is 29th in bench scoring this season while the Suns are seventh and only getting better. Luke Kennard, Collin Gillespie, and Jordan Goodwin are shooting the ball at an elite level so far this season, and if they continue to play well, the Suns can rely on them to put this game out of reach by the fourth quarter. Key to a Suns Win Against a team the Suns are far more talented than, the key is to play with the same energy and defensive effort they showed against the Nuggets. That level of play set the new standard for how this starting group should play, and if both the starters and the bench show up and take care of business, this game will be over long before the 48 minutes of game time are done. Prediction Suns cruise to a victory and win. Suns 117, Kings 95

stories.summary: Dallas looks to take advantage of a Splash-Bro-less Warriors team
stories.detailText: The Mavericks face the Golden State Warriors at home on Wednesday night. It will be the first meeting between former Michigan teammates Morez Johnson Jr. and Yaxel Lendeborg, but the story will be about both of these teams righting the ship. The Warriors have dropped their last two games without Stephen Curry and did not eclipse 100 points in either contest. The Mavericks have lost three in a row in embarrassing fashion and have to get back on track against a bad Warriors team. It should be a “get right” game for Dallas, if they can muster any effort at all. Before getting into our picks, here is how we stand this season, and what our daily picks are over on The Feed: Season to date Tyler: 5-3-0 (+$143) David: 7-1-0 (+$667) Game Details Dallas Mavericks (7-7) vs Golden State Warriors (8-6) Tipoff: 7:10 PM CST How to watch: The local broadcast will be handled by KFAA Channel 29, with the game also airing on sister stations throughout the Mavs’ regional viewership area. stories.summary: Resilience seemed to be a buzzword after the Lakers’ win Tuesday night
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CA - NOVEMBER 17: Ziaire Williams #11 and Quentin Grimes #5 of the Los Angeles Lakers smile after the game against the Charlotte Hornets on November 17, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Adam Pantozzi/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Following the Los Angeles Lakers’ come-from-behind victory over the Charlotte Hornets Tuesday night, head coach JJ Redick praised his team’s resiliency as the Lakers erased a 14-point fourth-quarter deficit to win, despite the absence of critical starters in Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler. Among those who elevated their game to mitigate the loss of Reaves and Kessler was Quentin Grimes, who recorded a career-high 47 points (16-of-24 shooting, 10-of-14 beyond the arc), six rebounds, three assists and one steal. His night was headlined by a game-tying triple in regulation and go-ahead free throws during overtime. QUENTIN GRIMES' 10TH THREE SENDS THE GAME INTO OT 🤯 HE'S GOT 45 POINTS! pic.twitter.com/Owfe0RTetV — NBA (@NBA) November 18, 2026 Grimes echoed his head coach’s message of resilience and thought Los Angeles’ gutsy win made clear this team’s identity. “I’m calling this one a statement game. This was a statement game for the team,” Grimes told reporters postgame . “We were down 18, so having guys know we’re shorthanded and being able to rally around everybody, not just by my scoring but coming together and trying to gut this win out. I feel like this was a big time statement game showing how hard we play and how resilient, how tough this team could be for later on in the season.” While Grimes stepped up considerably without Reaves, it seemed as though the entire rotation collectively worked together and helped soften the loss of a defensive presence like Kessler. This season, the Lakers are allowing 111.0 points per 100 possessions with Kessler on the floor and 118.4 points per 100 whenever he sits, per Cleaning the Glass. On Tuesday, a night Kessler didn’t play at all, they held the Hornets to a 110.8 offensive rating. Yes, Charlotte is the league’s 30th-ranked offense, generating a meager 105.3 points per 100 possessions, but Los Angeles still found a way to cobble together stops without its interior anchor — particularly in the second half — something it’s not often done through the first month of the year. That’s the sort of performance deserving of Grimes’ labels: resilient, tough and hard-playing. The Lakers return to the floor aiming for a 10th consecutive Wednesday night when the Utah Jazz stroll into Crypto.com Arena. A number of players, including Davion Mitchell , Nick Richards , Tim Hardaway Jr. and more posted about receiving a game-themed care package from Rockstar Games, PlayStation and luggage company Rimowa for GTA VI's release. It included custom controllers, consoles and, of course, a copy of the game. The care package came in a fitting color scheme -- Miami's Vice City pink and black alternate branding. Mitchell, who posted about the gift on his Instagram story, added a humorous caption: "I'm about to deactivate my account because I'm about to lock in," he wrote, adding saluting and laughing emojis. "It's up!!!" The Heat will face the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday night (7 p.m. EST, ESPN).

teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO -- Spurs guard Dylan Harper will miss Thursday's home game against the LA Clippers due to left hip soreness. Harper left San Antonio's 105-93 loss to Detroit on Tuesday with 53 seconds remaining after slipping on the court. Harper's feet slid out from under him as he stopped to plant on a pass from Stephon Castle with 1:07 remaining in the game. Harper fell and remained on the court as Ausar Thompson stole the pass, helping preserve the Pistons' victory that snapped San Antonio's 12-game winning streak. Harper remained on the court for about a minute before the action was stopped by a San Antonio foul. He was helped off the court by teammates and staff. Harper finished with 20 points, four rebounds and two assists in 35 minutes against Detroit. The second-year guard is averaging 18.4 points, 5.4 rebounds and 4.5 assists while shooting 50.5% from the field.
