stories.title: Niners' Nick Bosa on 4-game sack drought: 'Don't think I'm playing my best'
stories.summary: Niners star Nick Bosa acknowledged his performance this season, including four straight games with no sacks, hasn't been up to his usual standard.
stories.detailText: COLORADO SPRINGS, Colo. -- After failing to record a sack in his fourth straight game, San Francisco 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa acknowledged Wednesday that his performance this season has not been up to his usual standard. In the Niners' 46-40 win against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, Bosa played 34 defensive snaps in which he had a pass rush opportunity. He finished with no sacks, one quarterback hit and four pressures while also being called for three penalties, including two for jumping offside. It's the first time since Bosa entered the league in 2019 that he hasn't had a sack in four straight games in the same season. "I think in the past when I was younger, it would eat at me a lot more, just strictly the stat aspects," Bosa said after the Niners completed their first practice of the week at the Air Force Academy in preparation for this week's showdown with the Minnesota Vikings . "But now I'm really just focused on the people around me, and if I feel like I'm playing good football, then I really don't care much about the stats. But I don't think I'm playing my best football right now. So that's what gets to me more so than the actual stats." Bosa is still working his way back from multiple injuries. He missed all but three games in 2025 because of a torn ACL in his right knee. During training camp this year, Bosa participated in individual drills in the opening days but then missed most of the preseason before playing 70 snaps in the first two games of the season. But before the Niners played the Arizona Cardinals in Week 3, Bosa strained his calf while warming up during a Thursday walkthrough and missed the ensuing five games. Bosa said that injury was a result of overcompensation from his ACL recovery. Upon returning, Bosa has attempted to fit into new coordinator Raheem Morris' defensive scheme. The system isn't drastically different from what Bosa and other veteran Niners have played in, but has enough nuance that it takes some time to catch up. Bosa said Wednesday that he also could have done a better job being proactive about learning those details about Morris' defense. "I think there's a learning curve and ... a lot of guys haven't had many reps in the scheme so far," Bosa said. "I'm trying to break it down to the basics and just kind of get back. I missed a year and then missed camp. I kind of took for granted some of the things that I did automatically, and I thought I could just kind of coast and continue to do those things automatically and focus on other things. But I need to, especially with a newer defense, really hone in on the things that made me the player that I am." Asked for an example of something he needs to refocus on, Bosa pointed to doing a better job of setting his feet and getting off the ball at the snap, before stopping short of sharing too much for competitive reasons. "It takes time," Bosa said. "I'm not going to make excuses because nobody really cares. But I'm going to get better and I'm pretty confident in that physically and how I'm playing." A healthy and productive Bosa, even if not back to his 2022 Defensive Player of the Year level of play would be a boon for a Niners pass rush that has struggled to generate pressure and sacks of late. In the past three games, the Niners have just one sack and a pressure rate of 25.8% that is 31st in the league in that span. It hasn't been all bad this season for Bosa, who needs three sacks to pass Charles Haley for second-most in franchise history (66.5). If Bosa had played enough snaps to qualify, his 25% pass rush win rate would rank eighth in the NFL among edge rushers and 11th among all defenders. Niners coach Kyle Shanahan said he believes Bosa will continue to get healthier, knock off rust and acclimate to Morris' scheme as the year goes on. "I see Nick working his way back," Shanahan said. "I think that he has a number of plays that look just like Nick and I think he's had a few plays that doesn't. I think Nick's ready to go and I think he's definitely affecting the quarterback and doing some good things out there. ... I'm not worried about Nick. Nick's going to get better each week and he'll eventually get there."

stories.title: Cam Skattebo done with backflip celebration in wake of Aidan Hutchinson injury
stories.summary: Cam Skattebo has seen enough. The Giants RB says he is ending his backflip celebration in the wake of Aidan Hutchinson's season-ending injury.
stories.detailText: No flipping way. That's the message from New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo in regard to his famed touchdown celebration. Skattebo, who has never been one to shy away from contact or a moment to celebrate, saw all he needed to see when it came to Aidan Hutchinson's season-ending injury . The Detroit Lions ' star celebrated a sack of New England Patriots QB Drake Maye by jumping in the air. When Hutchinson landed, he suffered a torn ACL. And that was enough for Skattebo to retire his backflip celebration – at least for the time being. “It’s hard to see,” Skattebo told reporters, via the New York Post's Ryan Dunleavy , after Wednesday’s practice. “I’m saying yeah (no more). Mentally, I’m like, ‘I’m not doing that.’ That ain’t going to happen to me.” This isn't the first time that the running back's celebration has been a topic of discussion. Skattebo was seen on video backflipping multiple times last offseason, despite coming off a serious season-ending ankle injury in 2025. It got to a point where new head coach, John Harbaugh, was asked for his reaction. Harbaugh joked about the situation, saying in part, " Dude, at least stick it ." The 24-year-old brought the celebration back to the field in the Giants' season opener when he scored a touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys. At the time, he left the door open for a new celebration to emerge, but the backflip resurfaced again as recently as Week 10 against the Washington Commanders on "Thursday Night Football." So is the backflip done? Maybe for now. Or maybe not. Skattebo noted it could come back in a big moment, like if the Giants make the playoffs. In other words, Skattebo and the backflip are taking a break. History says they'll be back together soon enough though. stories.title: NFL slams NBC's Mike Florio, Chris Simms for 'offensive' Mike Vrabel joke
stories.summary: Mike Florio and Chris Simms made a joke at the expense of Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel that included a thinly veiled reference to Adolf Hitler.
stories.detailText: The NFL is not happy with one of its primary media partners. During a recent episode of "Pro Football Talk Live" on NBC Sports, Mike Florio and Chris Simms made a joke at the expense of New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel that included a thinly veiled reference to Adolf Hitler, although neither mentioned his name. "He got the German mustache to go along with that right now, too,” Simms said during a Nov. 17 edition of the show while discussing the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday in Munich, Germany. “So he was hitting all themes there over in Germany." “You gotta be careful trimming that thing," Florio said. “Yeah, if you’re in Germany, you gotta be careful trimming the sides of that thing." NBC Sports' Mike Florio makes Hitler joke about Patriots coach Mike Vrabel. 🔉: PFT Live with Mike Florio pic.twitter.com/EmJQeaq1tP — TMZ (@TMZ) November 18, 2026 Between a lot of laughs, Simms and Florio kept the bit going for a few more seconds, although an off-air producer must have appeared to wish the duo didn't go down that road. "It was eighty years ago," Florio said. "Let us have some fun, for crying out loud." The exchange did not sit well within NFL headquarters. “We found the remarks inappropriate and offensive,” the NFL said in a statement to USA TODAY Sports from executive vice president of communications, policy and public affairs Jeff Miller Both Florio and Simms contribute to NBC's elbow coverage of "Sunday Night Football." Simms had previously been part of "Football Night in America" but was removed from the show this offseason. The duo apologized Thursday. “On yesterday’s (Nov. 17) PFT Live show, we made comments that some found offensive and we apologize,” Simms and Florio said in a joint statement via NBC Sports . stories.detailText: Staying up to date on NFL injury news is of the utmost importance for fantasy football success. The article below tracks all fantasy-relevant players currently listed on their team's injury report and provides fantasy managers with actionable recommendations as new information rolls in. Check back for updates from Tuesday through Saturday. Don’t forget: Check out the Rotoworld player news feed for all the latest news, notes, and transactions around the league. **UPDATED AS OF WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 18 AT 8:15 PM ET** AFC East ◆ Buffalo Bills Dalton Kincaid - TE (thumb/ankle) Kincaid begins Week 11 sidelined. Impact: Likely none, though the Bills will employ a run-heavy approach against the Dolphins. Joshua Palmer - WR (hamstring) Palmer managed only seven offensive snaps in Week 8 before departing with an aggravation of the hamstring injury he has battled since Week 4. He was placed on injured reserve. Impact: Not much, honestly. Palmer has played sparingly this season in a situational role, although his absence could leave room for Skyler Bell to be active for the third time this season. The Bills also activated Tyrell Shavers (knee) from the reserve/physically unable to perform list . He could join the wide receiver rotation but does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues. ◆ Miami Dolphins De’Von Achane - RB (knee) Achane suffered a torn ACL in the team's Week 3 loss to the Chiefs, ending his season. Impact: Achane's unfortunate season-ending injury creates opportunity for Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright . The timing of the injury makes it likely that Achane is able to fully recover before the start of the 2027 regular season. Malik Willis - QB (groin) The Dolphins placed Willis on injured reserve in Week 10. He will be eligible to return in Week 14, but Willis is seeking a second opinion after the injury progressed into his abdomen. Season-ending surgery is possible , although the team has yet to decide if or when surgery would take place. Impact : Kyle McCord 's installation as the team's starter hurts all involved. Until we see how McCord fares in this system, only Ollie Gordon is a safe FLEX starter. Chris Bell - WR (knee) Bell is listed as doubtful for Week 10 against the Colts. He is day-to-day entering Week 11. Impact: Bell has largely been unable to get anything going during his rookie season, with the team leaning more heavily on Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas ( shoulder ), who was limited to begin Week 11. Bell's status could afford Kevin Coleman Jr. additional opportunities, although the low-volume Miami pass offense remains unlikely to support more than one pass catcher, now playing with a backup quarterback in Kyle McCord . ◆ New England Patriots Drake Maye - QB (ankle) Maye is believed to have suffered a fractured ankle , an injury that would sideline him for the remainder of the 2026 season . Impact: As of Tuesday, the team continues to gather more information on the injury sustained in the first half of the Week 10 loss to the Lions. The team is also reportedly reaching out to quarterbacks as they look to right a sinking ship following consecutive losses for the first time in head coach Mike Vrabel's tenure. More to come on this developing story. Suffice to say, the fantasy value of the primary skill position players in New England takes a significant hit for the remainder of the year. Romeo Doubs - WR (shoulder) Doubs was placed on injured reserve following a shoulder injury sustained in Week 6. He will miss the next four games, at minimum. Impact: The Patriots have now played only 33 offensive snaps with both Doubs and A.J. Brown on the field together this season after Doubs was injured on his second offensive snap in Week 6. Brown returned from injured reserve in Week 6 and should have the runway to return WR1 numbers while Doubs remains sidelined. A.J. Brown - WR (hamstring) Brown missed Week 8 and Week 9 with ankle and knee issues before returning for Week 10 against the Lions, only to pick up a hamstring injury. The team is reportedly gathering more information during their Week 11 bye. Impact: DeMario Douglas , Kyle Williams , Mack Hollins , and Kyle Williams led the team in snaps and routes in the absence of Brown in Week 9, with none of the bunch consistent fantasy producers. Fantasy managers are likely forced to wait until more information is released to gauge Brown's expected status in Week 12. TreVeyon Henderson - RB (illness) Henderson was placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 10 and will miss the next four games, at minimum. Impact: Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner are likely to form a one-two punch in the absence of Henderson, with Stevenson the favorite to lead the team in opportunities and snaps. Stevenson can be viewed as a volume-backed RB2 for the time being. ◆ New York Jets Geno Smith - QB (ankle) Smith departed the team's Week 10 loss with an ankle injury. Follow-up testing confirmed the injury is not considered serious but his status for Week 11 against the Chiefs is in doubt. He was officially limited on Wednesday. Impact: The fantasy upside of all primary skill position players for the Jets would take a significant hit should Smith be unavailable against the Chiefs. Fantasy managers will want to monitor this situation closely in the coming days. Omar Cooper - WR (ankle) Cooper aggravated the same ankle injury he has been dealing with for multiple weeks in Week 10, placing his status in doubt for Week 11. He was sidelined to begin the week . Impact: Target volume would likely concentrate further on Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell should Cooper be unable to play against the Chiefs. Isaiah Williams ( ribs ) is also hurt. AFC North ◆ Baltimore Ravens Lamar Jackson - QB (thumb) Jackson returned from an ankle injury in Week 8 and made it all of one offensive snap before suffering a thumb injury that is likely to sideline him for the remainder of the regular season. Impact: Jackson's absence is the biggest hit to the fantasy value of alpha receiver Zay Flowers , who falls to a mid-range WR2 in rest of season rankings. Recent signee Jacoby Brissett is expected to start under center in Week 10 . Tyler Huntley - QB (toe) Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury in the team's Week 8 loss to the Bills. Impact: See above. Durham Smythe - TE (Achilles) Smythe suffered a torn Achilles in the team's Week 4 win over the Titans. His season is done. Impact: It was Matt Hibner who saw the largest increase in snaps following Smythe's departure in Week 4, making it unlikely we see veteran Mark Andrews in a more robust role. ◆ Cincinnati Bengals Andrei Iosivas - WR (thumb) The Bengals placed Iosivas on injured reserve in Week 3. The team activated his 21-day practice window this week but he is listed as doubtful to play in Week 10 against the Steelers. Impact: Wide receivers Colbie Young and Dohnte Meyers will duke it out for the No. 3 wide receiver role for at least the next four weeks. Meyers can be added in 14-team leagues, though his upside is questionable. Erick All - TE (knee) All suffered a torn ACL in Week 7. He was placed on injured reserve Tuesday and will miss the remainder of the regular season. Impact: All loses yet another season in devastating fashion after suffering his third torn ACL. His absence could provide a slight uptick in snap rate and route participation for Mike Gesicki , although he will be a difficult weekly start for as long as both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins remain healthy. ◆ Cleveland Browns Raheim Sanders - RB (hip) The Browns placed Sanders on injured reserve in Week 6 . Impact: He will be eligible to return after four games missed. ◆ Pittsburgh Steelers Michael Pittman - WR (foot) Pittman was limited on Wednesday before being seen using a scooter in the locker room after practice . It was then revealed that Pittman aggravated his foot injury. The Steelers placed him on injured reserve late in Week 5 . Pittman was limited to begin Week 11 after the Steelers designated him to return. Impact: Pittman's potential return could lower Germie Bernard 's target share. Head coach Mike McCarthy said Monday that the team is hopeful Pittman and Wilson can return for Week 11. Roman Wilson - WR (finger) The Steelers designated Wilson to return from his Week 5 finger injury in Week 11. He is practicing fully . Impact: See above. AFC South ◆ Houston Texans Woody Marks - RB (concussion) Marks will not play in Week 11 after suffering a concussion in Week 10. Impact: David Montgomery is tentatively expected to return from injury and should see the bulk of the opportunities out of the backfield, with Emari Demercado now on hand to operate in the primary change of pace role. Montgomery is a viable RB2, if active. Marvin Harrison Jr. - WR (hamstring) Harrison will miss another game after injuring his hamstring in practice in Week 10. Impact: Hamstring injuries can be tricky for wide receivers. Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson would mildly benefit with Harrison sidelined. Jaylin Noel - WR (toe) Noel suffered a turf toe injury in Week 7. The Texans placed him on injured reserve in Week 8. He is expected to miss the remainder of the regular season. Impact: Tank Dell and recent acquisition Marvin Harrison Jr. would be in line to benefit. Harrison should be added in 12-team formats. David Montgomery - RB (groin) Head coach DeMeco Ryans said in Week 5 that Montgomery is " week-to-week " with a groin injury. He is set to return for the Texans' Thursday Night Football game against the Colts. Impact: Montgomery is a volume-backed RB2 if he returns for Week 11. Emari Demercado would fill those shoes should Montgomery miss. Jawhar Jordan - RB (undisclosed) The Texans placed Jordan on injured reserve in Week 7 . Impact: Jordan prevented Marks from handling a full-time role in Week 6. Dare Ogunbowale will probably do the same while Montgomery is sidelined. Jayden Higgins - WR (knee) Higgins saw his 2026 season taken from him due to a torn ACL suffered in camp. Impact: It's a massive blow to a Texans team that was counting on Higgins taking another step forward in his Sophomore campaign. The team traded for Kayshon Boutte in the wake of the injury and then added Marvin Harrison Jr. in a deal with the Cardinals ahead of Week 6. ◆ Indianapolis Colts Alec Pierce - WR (heel) Pierce aggravated the injury that required offseason surgery in Week 2. The Colts placed him on injured reserve in Week 3 . He will attempt to avoid surgery by rehabbing his injured heel. Head coach Shane Steichen said he is unsure whether Pierce will play again this season . Impact: Tyler Warren is the de facto top option through the air for the remainder of the season. Anthony Gould - WR (toe) Gould is questionable for Week 11 . Impact: He is not fantasy-relevant in 12-team leagues, but losing him would further condense the pass-catching corps. ◆ Jacksonville Jaguars Bayshul Tuten - RB (ankle/foot) Tuten played in Week 9 without practicing. He played in Week 10 while practicing minimally, and he begins Week 11 limited . Impact: His health is improving. Tuten is an RB1. Chris Rodriguez - RB (hand) Rodriguez played through the injury in Week 9 and remained limited early in Week 10. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Titans. Rodriguez remains limited in practice , but will play. Impact : He is only a bench stash. Jakobi Meyers - WR (ankle) Meyers remains limited in practice . Impact: None. ◆ Tennessee Titans Carnell Tate - WR (shoulder) Tate begins Week 11 limited , and is tentatively on track to return from his multi-week injury. Impact: Tate would be in the WR2/3 range against the Cowboys, if active. Wan’Dale Robinson - WR (ankle) Robinson suffered an ankle injury in Week 10 and will be sidelined for the rest of the year . Impact: Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike enter the matchup-based FLEX tier. Tyjae Spears - RB (knee) Spears has been nursing a knee injury for weeks and begins Week 11 limited . Impact: Spears does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. AFC West ◆ Denver Broncos Jaylen Waddle - WR (concussion) Waddle suffered a concussion in the team's Week 9 win over the Panthers. He is practicing in full for Week 11 . Impact: Waddle returns to the volatile WR3 tier. RJ Harvey - RB (knee) Harvey popped on the injury report Thursday with a knee injury and was ruled out for Week 8 on Friday. He was placed on injured reserve Saturday and will miss the next four weeks, at minimum. Impact: Jonah Coleman is an RB2, operating as the team's starter. ◆ Kansas City Chiefs Kenneth Walker - RB (groin) Walker was added to the injury report for Week 10's Friday practice and was ultimately ruled out for Week 10 against the Falcons. He remains sidelined to begin Week 11. Impact: Emmett Johnson is an RB1 for as long as Walker is sidelined. We expect Walker to be held out in Week 11. Tyquan Thornton - WR (ankle) Thornton suffered a devastating ankle injury due to a hip-drop tackle in Week 4. He is reportedly set to undergo surgery within the week and will miss 12-16 weeks. Impact: The team has lost all ability to attack downfield without Thornton, meaning our fantasy interest should be confined to those with expected volume. ◆ Las Vegas Raiders Brock Bowers - TE (ankle) Bowers picked up an ankle injury in the team's Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. He did not practice the following Wednesday . Impact: Head coach Klint Kubiak relayed Monday that the injury is not considered serious, though he tends to downplay injuries. Michael Mayer is tentatively in line to start. ◆ Los Angeles Chargers Ladd McConkey - WR (back) McConkey reportedly experienced back spasms during warmups for Week 9 and ultimately did not play . He did not play in Week 10. McConkey was limited to begin Week 11. Impact: McConkey would be a WR3 if active. NFC East ◆ Dallas Cowboys Jake Ferguson - TE (ankle) Ferguson departed the team's Week 9 win with an ankle injury. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday that the veteran tight end is "expected to miss time." He was ruled out for Week 10 and remains sidelined in Week 11. Impact: Brevin Spann-Ford is on hand to handle primary tight end duties. He is not a recommended streaming option outside of the deepest leagues. Malik Davis - RB (hip) Davis was placed on injured reserve and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Impact: The Cowboys released both Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah at roster cuts and now have only Emari Demercado on the active roster behind starter Javonte Williams . Expect Israel Abanikanda to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad for Week 2, while Williams appears likely to see all the work he can handle against the Commanders. Williams is a locked-in RB1. Tyler Goodson - RB (ankle/knee) The team sent Goodson to injured reserve Saturday. Impact: The Cowboys have struggled with depth in the backfield all season, which takes another blow in the absence of Goodson. Israel Abanikanda was signed to the active roster and will serve as the primary change of pace option behind Javonte Williams in the immediate future. Williams remains a locked-in RB2 with one of the more robust roles in the league. ◆ New York Giants Jaxson Dart - QB (knee) Dart injured his MCL, PCL and meniscus on the team's first possession of Monday Night Football against the Rams. He will undergo surgery to address the MCL and meniscus and miss the rest of the regular season. Giants head coach John Harbaugh said it is possible for Dart to return in the postseason, although this is unlikely. Impact: Backup Jameis Winston was benched in favor of recent acquisition J.J. McCarthy in the second half of their loss to the Saints. Head coach John Harbaugh confirmed McCarthy as the starter for Week 7. Cam Skattebo - RB (hamstring) Skattebo is practicing in full for Week 11. Impact: None. He is a low-end RB1 with six teams on bye. ◆ Philadelphia Eagles Dameon Pierce - RB (undisclosed) Pierce was injured on a kick return in the fourth quarter of the team's Week 7 loss to the Cowboys. He was placed on injured reserve the following Wednesday . Impact: See above. DeVonta Smith - WR (hamstring) Smith has repeatedly aggravated the hamstring strain he initially injured in August. He was limited to begin Week 11 and told reporters he is 100 percent healthy . Impact: Dontayvion Wicks ( ankle ) was also limited. Both players are tentatively on track to play in Week 11, though only Smith needs to be in 12-team lineups. Tank Bigsby - RB (core) See above. Impact: See above. Jalen Hurts - QB (blood clots) Team doctors discovered a blood clot in Hurts' calf. He was ruled out for Week 6 and could be looking at an extended absence. He was placed on injured reserve on Saturday after more clots were found in his lungs. Impact: Hurts is currently sidelined indefinitely. Tanner McKee enters the starting lineup under center following the release of Andy Dalton. The Philadelphia offense could be in trouble in the immediate future considering the sheer number of injuries. Will Shipley - RB (foot) Shipley reportedly suffered a partial tear of the plantar fascia in his foot in Week 5. He resumed practicing in a limited capacity in Week 11 . Impact: Shipley can be stashed. Saquon Barkley - RB (hamstring) Barkley is no longer listed with a back injury and is practicing in full post- bye . Impact: His health is improving. Barkley is an RB1. ◆ Washington Commanders Terry McLaurin - WR (knee) McLaurin suffered a season-ending patellar tendon rupture in Week 6. Impact: Stefon Diggs will likely serve as the de facto No. 1 wide receiver moving forward. Jaylin Lane - WR (ankle) Lane suffered a dislocated ankle and fracture in Week 4 and is likely done for the season. Impact: Minimal. Lane was primarily a special teams contributor. Jacory Croskey-Merritt - RB (groin) Croskey-Merritt was unable to practice this week and ruled out for Week 6 against the 49ers. The team then placed him on injured reserve . He was designated to return from injured reserve Monday . Impact: Croskey-Merritt should resume his lead-rushing role upon returning. Jeremy McNichols - RB (foot) McNichols suffered a foot injury in Week 8 and was placed on injured reserve in Week 9. Impact: Rachaad White and veteran Austin Ekeler are suddenly the only two healthy backs on the Washington roster, neither of whom is an overly exciting fantasy option on a struggling offense. White is the preferred option and could be started as a viable FLEX, should McNichols miss time. NFC North ◆ Chicago Bears Kyle Monangai - RB (toe) Monangai is practicing in full for Week 11. Impact: Monangai should return to a split backfield with D'Andre Swift . Monangai is FLEX-viable against the Saints. Cole Kmet - TE (knee) Kmet suffered a season-ending knee injury in the team's Thursday Night Football win over the Patriots. Impact: Expect Sam Roush to serve as the team's TE2 for the remainder of the season, while second-year tight end Colston Loveland should continue his recent ascension back into TE1 territory. ◆ Detroit Lions Isiah Pacheco - RB (back) Pacheco was placed on injured reserve to start the season. General Manager Brad Holmes said he "hopes Pacheco returns this season." Impact: Well, that doesn't sound great. There appears to be something more insidious going on with Pacheco's back than initially thought. Lions coach Dan Campbell said running backs Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki could split touches behind Jahmyr Gibbs . Saylors appears to be the first player up. Gibbs handled an absurd 34 opportunities, of 37 total running back opportunities, in the team's Week 1, overtime win over the Saints ◆ Green Bay Packers Josh Jacobs - RB (finger) Jacobs suffered a fractured finger in the team's Week 9 win over the Patriots. He will miss two-to-three weeks after undergoing surgery . Impact: Kaleb Johnson is reportedly the first in line for lead back duties in his absence. Jayden Reed - WR (neck) Reed suffered a scary-looking neck injury that required stabilization in the team's Week 2 win over the Jets. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said on Tuesday that it is " way too early " to determine whether Reed will play again in 2026. That said, he was not placed on injured reserve ahead of their Week 3 contest. He will reportedly undergo surgery . Impact: Beyond the football implications, it is good to hear Reed avoided any life-altering injuries in Week 2. Skyy Moore and Bo Melton are likely to soak up additional snaps, although volume is most likely to concentrate on Christian Watson , Matthew Golden , and Tucker Kraft . ◆ Minnesota Vikings Kyler Murray - QB (hamstring) Murray was reportedly “slowed” by a hamstring injury in the team’s Week 8 loss to the Lions and is undergoing further tests to identify the severity. Those tests revealed a Grade 2 hamstring strain, which is likely to sideline the newly anointed backup quarterback for 3-4 weeks. Impact: Murray can be dropped. Carson Wentz ( ankle ) is also ailing. T.J. Hockenson - TE (wrist/chest) Hockenson missed Week 10, but was limited to begin Week 11. Impact: Jauan Jennings remains sidelined and Jordan Addison is listed as questionable after banging his thumb in practice Friday. Justin Jefferson could see all the volume he can handle, although his per-target efficiency likely improves with Addison on the field in a downfield role. Jordan Addison - WR (thumb) Addison will undergo surgery to address a thumb injury sustained in practice and will miss multiple weeks, although he avoided injured reserve . Impact: Tai Felton and Myles Price will serve as the top two pass catchers behind Justin Jefferson for as long as Addison and Jauan Jennings remain sidelined. Neither is an overly exciting fantasy option. Jauan Jennings - WR (calf) Jennings is practicing in full for Week 11. Impact: Jennings could be a WR4/5 against his former 49ers squad this week. Don’t forget: Check out the Rotoworld player news feed for all the latest news, notes, and transactions around the league. NFC South ◆ Atlanta Falcons Brian Robinson - RB (hamstring) Robinson was placed on injured reserve on Saturday. Impact: In a shocking development, Robinson went from limited showings in practice with a questionable designation for Week 9 to injured reserve, with the potential that the veteran backup aggravated his ailment sometime during practice to end the week. He will miss the next four games, at minimum. Khalil Herbert should continue as the top change-of-pace option behind Bijan Robinson , the former of whom is not fantasy-viable. Zachariah Branch - WR (hamstring) Branch was ruled out for Week 9 against the Bengals early in the week. He remains sidelined in Week 10. Impact: Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts should continue dominating targets. ◆ Carolina Panthers Jonathan Brooks - RB (groin) Brooks aggravated the groin injury that forced him to miss the end of camp. The Panthers placed him on injured reserve in Week 3. The Panthers designated him to return in Week 10 . He is practicing in full for Week 11. Impact: Chuba Hubbard remains in the volume-driven RB1 tier. Brooks is a moderately worthwhile stash. Bryce Young - WR (foot) Young continues to practice fully through lower-body injuries . Impact: He's a QB2 with upside, though Darren Waller ( knee ) is banged up. ◆ New Orleans Saints Jordyn Tyson - WR (chest) Tyson injured his chest in Week 10, but was limited to begin Week 11. Impact: Likely none. ◆ Tampa Bay Buccaneers Baker Mayfield - QB (leg) Mayfield sustained a foot strain in the team's Week 10 loss to the Bears and was sidelined to begin Week 11. Impact: The team signed former Falcons quarterback Cooper Rush Monday, hinting at a likely absence for Mayfield against the Lions. An absence would greatly impact the fantasy upside of all remaining Buccaneers skill position players. Jalen McMillan - WR (knee) McMillan suffered a sprained PCL in his first game action of the season in Week 3. The team placed him on injured reserve Monday, with an expected absence of 6-8 weeks. Impact: Not much change considering he made his season debut in Week 3, although rookie Ted Hurst should remain in the starting lineup. NFC West ◆ Arizona Cardinals Jeremiyah Love - RB (ankle) The team placed Love on injured reserve after yet another ankle injury sustained in Week 8. Impact: Bam Knight (concussion) resumed practicing in Week 10. Tyler Allgeier likely returns to a receiving/rotational rushing role. Jalen Brooks - WR (wrist) Brooks had emergency surgery on his wrist and will miss the remainder of the regular season. Impact: The team signed veteran Zay Jones Tuesday in an associated move. Expect volume to continue to remain heavily concentrated on Michael Wilson and Trey McBride . Elijah Higgins is notable for DFS purposes. Gardner Minshew - QB (elbow) Minshew is feared to have torn his UCL in the team's Week 9 loss to the Seahawks. Impact: Minshew appears likely to be placed on injured reserve in the coming days, leaving rookie Carson Beck to start under center for the remainder of the season. Michael Wilson - WR (neck) Wilson suffered a neck injury in Week 9 that will end his 2026 season. Impact: The Cardinals are now without their starting quarterback, second-string quarterback, alpha wide receiver, secondary and tertiary wide receiver, and starting running back as they head into the second half of a lost season. Trey McBride should soak up all the volume he can handle, with that volume now coming from rookie Carson Beck . ◆ Los Angeles Rams Terrance Ferguson - TE (hamstring) Ferguson appeared to be on track to be activated from injured reserve after logging a full practice to end the week, but was ruled out for Week 9 with a new hamstring injury. He will miss multiple games . Impact: Fantasy managers will have to continue to wait for the return of Ferguson. Davante Adams - WR (hamstring) The Rams placed Adams on i njured reserve with a ruptured hamstring tendon. He underwent surgery in Week 8. The team is targeting a Week 13 return . Impact: The Rams will employ run-heavy game plans in the coming weeks. Puka Nacua - WR (knee/toe) Nacua suffered PCL and MCL sprains, plus a turf toe injury, on the final play from scrimmage in the team's Week 9 win over the Commanders. Nacua was placed on injured reserve Friday. Impact: See above. ◆ San Francisco 49ers Mike Evans - WR (Achilles) Evans aggravated his Achilles injury in Week 6 and is expected to " miss some time ." He remains sidelined early in Week 11. Impact: The entire pass-catching corps for the 49ers continues to be in flux. The addition of veteran Keenan Allen at the trade deadline aimed to stem the bleeding, although Evans could return in Week 11 against the Vikings. Christian Kirk - WR (knee) Kirk was limited on Wednesday . He was ruled out for Week 9 on Friday and placed on injured reserve on Saturday. Impact: None. De’Zhaun Stribling - WR (ankle) Stribling suffered an ankle injury in the team's Week 1 win over the Rams. The 49ers placed him on injured reserve in Week 2 after he underwent surgery to repair a deltoid ligament tear. He is expected to return in 10 weeks. Stribling worked with trainers , for the first time, off to the side early in Week 11. Impact: The Athletic's Matt Barrows believes Demarcus Robinson will be the primary beneficiary. George Ricky Pearsall - WR (knee) Pearsall was placed on season-ending injured reserve. Impact: Pearsall will miss the entirety of the 2026 season. ◆ Seattle Seahawks Sam Darnold - QB (quad/ribs) The Seahawks ruled out Darnold for Week 9 on Wednesday . He was also ruled out for Week 10. Impact: Recent reports indicate Darnold could return following the team's Week 11 bye. George Holani - RB (knee) Holani is week-to-week with an MCL sprain as of Week 11. Impact: Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price will split backfield touches.

stories.title: Chargers-Jets Injury Report: Ladd McConkey returns to practice
stories.summary: Ladd McConkey returned to practice in a limited fashion after back spasms kept him sidelined for all of Week 10.
stories.detailText: EL SEGUNDO, CALIFORNIA - JULY 30: Ladd McConkey #15 of the Los Angeles Chargers runs with a reception during the Los Angeles Chargers Training Camp at The Bolt on July 30, 2026 in El Segundo, California. (Photo by Kevin Terrell/Getty Images) | Getty Images After backs spasms kept sidelined for the past two games, wide receiver Ladd McConkey returned to practice on Wednesday but participated in a limited fashion. He was one of five players who logged limited practices, joining cornerback Donte Jackson (groin), defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe (ankle), offensive lineman Trey Pipkins (knee), and safety Kendall Williamson (calf). wednesday's injury report for week 11 vs NYJ pic.twitter.com/PLfegFap4H — Los Angeles Chargers (@chargers) November 19, 2026 The six remaining players on the injury report were all DNPs. Edge rusher Khalil Mack received his usual veteran’s rest day to begin the new week, but the other five players who worked off to the side were cornerback Isas Waxter (ankle), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (hamstring), cornerback Rodney Shelley (ankle), tight end Charlie Kolar (concussion), and linebacker Daiyan Henley (knee). Henley played 61 of 69 snaps against the Ravens on Monday night and Jim Harbaugh told reporters earlier Wednesday he would sit out practice with knee soreness. Pipkins’ return could be something to watch should he be activated off of injured reserve this week. Harbaugh told reporters that rookie Logan Taylor would remain the starter after a standout performance against the Ravens. If right guard Cole Strange continues to underperform, there may be a chance Pipkins could relieve him of his duties. Kayode Awosika, who is now healthy, would also be a name to watch for that scenario, as well.

stories.title: Skip Bayless pours cold water on Troy Aikman-Cowboys reunion: ex-QB ‘would be a threat’
stories.summary: The rumblings come as Aikman’s broadcasting future remains in question.
stories.detailText: Skip Bayless isn’t buying the idea that Jerry Jones could bring in Troy Aikman to help him run the Cowboys. On the “ Double Coverage Podcast ,” Bayless commented on host Zach Hirsch’s suggestion that Jones might consider bringing on Aikman, Deion Sanders or Jason Witten to help lead the franchise. “The problem with everything you just said is all three of those names would be threats to Jerry’s stature,” Bayless said . “He’s the face of the franchise. He’s the most famous or infamous owner in all of sports. And he loves to sit up there on his throne peering down on his Cowboys and all the TV close-ups, and he just doesn’t want a threat. Troy, Troy would be a threat.” ESPN journalist Skip Bayless attends the IAVA 7th Annual Heroes Gala at Cipriani 42nd Street in New York City, Nov. 12, 2013. Michael Loccisano The rumblings come as Aikman’s broadcasting future remains in question. He remains without an extension with ESPN to call “Monday Night Football,” though longtime partner Joe Buck signed a massive deal earlier this year, which stirred reports of a feud between the pair . ESPN seems willing to move on from Aikman after this season, which will end after the network airs the Super Bowl for the first time in its history. Aikman has often expressed interest in taking on a front office role and an eagerness to go back to the Cowboys . Jones recently said that interest in working with his former quarterback is reciprocated . However, Jones’ and Aikman’s clashing philosophies on running a team have shown in the past. Jones has minimized the importance of a big investment in a head coach, while Aikman recently said that should he become an executive, he would immediately offer the 49ers anything they wanted to get Kyle Shanahan. Joe Buck, left, and Troy Aikman look on before an NFC Wild Card playoff game between the Dallas Cowboys and Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Tampa, Fla., Jan. 16, 2023. Getty Images It wouldn’t be Aikman’s first experience in a front office, as he’s worked for the Dolphins as a consultant since January. Aikman assisted in the search for Miami’s new general manager and head coach. Rumors of a rift between Aikman and Bayless have swirled in the past, especially following the release of Bayless’s book and his hiring by Fox Sports in 2016, but in 2024, Bayless said their relationship was “great” and the two spoke regularly.

stories.title: Buccaneers at Lions: Initial injury report for Week 11
stories.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers returned from their bye week and began preparations for their Week 11 matchup against the Detroit Lions on Wednesday, with much of the attention surrounding the health of quarterback Baker Mayfield. Tampa Bay listed six players on its initial injury report, including two who did not participat…
stories.detailText: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers returned from their bye week and began preparations for their Week 11 matchup against the Detroit Lions on Wednesday, with much of the attention surrounding the health of quarterback Baker Mayfield. Tampa Bay listed six players on its initial injury report , including two who did not participate in practice. Mayfield (foot/right thumb) was held out of Wednesday’s session after suffering an injury to his foot and ankle area during the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Chicago Bears. The veteran quarterback had reportedly been wearing a walking boot periodically throughout the bye week but was seen without one Wednesday while observing practice in street clothes. Head coach Todd Bowles offered somewhat encouraging news regarding Mayfield’s recovery, saying the quarterback has made progress and is doing considerably better than he was a week ago. However, as reported by Buccaneers senior writer Scott Smith , the team will wait until Friday to make a determination on his availability against Detroit. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels took first-team reps Wednesday and would once again be called upon should Mayfield be unable to play. The Buccaneers also promoted quarterback Easton Stick to the active roster earlier this week and signed veteran Cooper Rush to their practice squad. Aside from Mayfield, safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) was the only other Buccaneer held out of practice Wednesday. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee), who missed Tampa Bay’s game against Chicago, was a limited participant. Cornerback Josh Hayes (knee), tight end Cade Otton (thumb) and left tackle Tristan Wirfs (toe) participated fully. Hayes returned to practice Wednesday, opening his 21-day activation window from injured reserve. For Detroit, center Cade Mays (ankle) was the only player listed as a non-participant. Cornerbacks D.J. Reed (hip) and Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (shoulder) were among six players listed as limited, while safety Kerby Joseph (knee) was listed as a full participant. The Lions conducted a walkthrough Wednesday, meaning their participation designations were estimates. All eyes will remain on Mayfield throughout the remainder of the week as the Buccaneers look to avoid playing without their starting quarterback for the fourth time this season. The Buccaneers and Lions are scheduled to kick off Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS.

stories.summary: "PFT Live" hosts Mike Florio and Chris Simms were called out by the NFL for 'inappropriate and offensive' comments about Mike Vrabel's mustache that included thinly veiled references to Hitler.
stories.detailText: NBC Sports hosts Mike Florio, left, and Chris Simms broadcast from the 2025 NFL annual meetings in Palm Beach, Fla. (Phelan M. Ebenhack / Associated Press) “PFT Live” hosts Mike Florio and Chris Simms have apologized after being called out by the NFL for making thinly veiled references to Adolf Hitler while joking about Patriots coach Mike Vrabel ’s mustache and the team’s recent game in Munich. “On yesterday’s (Nov. 17) PFT Live show, we made comments that some found offensive and we apologize,” Florio and Simms said in a one-sentence, joint statement released by NBC Sports on Wednesday afternoon. A day earlier, the hosts were discussing the Patriots on the air when Simms made a comment about Vrabel’s “German mustache.” “If you’re in Germany, you gotta be careful about trimming the sides of that thing,” Florio joked. Read more: Fox Sports settles freelance workers’ wage claims in lawsuit that also accused Skip Bayless of harassment “Exactly right,” Simms responded. “‘Hey, who’s that going down the street over there? He put on a few pounds.” Neither of them mentioned the Nazi-era German dictator by name. Nonetheless, an off-camera producer apparently expressed some concerns over the nature of the discussion. “Gary’s groaning,” a still-laughing Florio said. “It’s funny, Gary! It was 80 years ago. Let us have some fun, for crying out loud.” The NFL was not amused. Read more: ESPN analyst and former NFL coach Rex Ryan charged with running over the feet of pedestrians in Nashville “We found the remarks inappropriate and offensive,” NFL executive vice president for communications and public affairs Jeff Miller said in a statement Wednesday morning. The NFL has reached out to NBC Sports regarding the matter, according to a league source unauthorized to discuss the matter publicly. NBC Sports put out a statement Wednesday afternoon. Read more: Britt McHenry says 'truly vile' comment sparked drink-throwing incident: 'I was sticking up for myself' “On yesterday’s (Nov. 17) PFT Live show, there were statements made that were inappropriate,” the network said. “Mike and Chris have apologized.” A longtime sports journalist, Florio started the “ ProFootballTalk ” website in 2001 and sold exclusive rights to its content to NBC in 2009. He has since become a fixture in the network’s football coverage, appearing weekly on “Football Night in America” and weighing in as needed as a top NFL insider. “ PFT Live ” is housed on NBC’s Peacock platform, with episodes five days a week. stories.title: Ravens' Humphrey apologizes for quip that Baltimore 'best at making criminals'
stories.summary: Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey apologized Wednesday for the derogatory comment he recently made about Baltimore on his podcast.
stories.detailText: OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Outspoken Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey apologized for the derogatory comment he made about the city of Baltimore on his recent podcast. On an episode of "The Marlon Humphrey Show" released Wednesday, Humphrey took a swipe at the city when asked what Baltimore was best at making. After first mentioning "The Star-Spangled Banner" and National Bohemian beer, Humphrey quipped, "They're best at making criminals." After Wednesday's practice, Humphrey said he regretted those remarks. "I would like to apologize for some comments on my podcast I had to the city of Baltimore," Humphrey said. "As you guys know, I've been here my whole career. Spent lots of offseasons here. Welcomed a son here and I'm an investor in the city. And obviously, I do know the effect that words have and just like to apologize for those comments." Humphrey received heavy fan backlash on social media Wednesday afternoon. The podcast episode featuring Humphrey's "criminals" comment has since been deleted from his YouTube page. Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott acknowledged Humphrey's apology in a statement posted to social media , but noted, "a verbal apology is not enough. Baltimore is a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives and to have someone that looks like them who wears a Baltimore Ravens jersey relegate them to becoming criminals cuts deeper. "I wonder how he would feel if prominent Baltimoreans used their platforms to imply that Baltimore once produced great defensive backs but we have recently lost our way." Scott then added, "They wouldn't do that because our team and city are supposed to be united as one. Baltimore versus the world." Scott concluded his post by inviting Humphrey to sit down with him and some Baltimore citizens "who have re-entered into our community and are now preventing others from making the mistakes they made." Humphrey, 30, is in his 10th season with Baltimore and is the longest-tenured defensive player on the Ravens. The No. 16 selection in the 2017 draft by Baltimore, Humphrey has been to four Pro Bowls, which are the most by a Ravens cornerback. In recent years, Humphrey has struggled and has drawn the ire of fans. This season, he has given up an NFL-worst 313 yards in coverage in the fourth quarter. Asked if he understood why fans would be upset with this comment even if he was joking, Humphrey replied, "Yeah, I just apologized ... and that won't really happen again." Humphrey is in the final year of a five-year, $97.5 million extension. His $26.276 million salary cap hit is the largest for any cornerback in 2026. Humphrey's slight at Baltimore comes at a time when the franchise is dealing with one of its worst stretches in its history. The Ravens (4-6) have lost five straight, including a 23-20 loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers on Monday. Baltimore has also lost seven of its past eight games at home. Ravens coach Jesse Minter said he would keep any conversations with Humphrey about this matter private. "Just speaking for myself, I love this city," Minter said. "I know what this city means to me and my family. I take a lot of pride in being here. It's a great city with a bunch of great people. We desperately want to represent this city the right way by how we play most importantly." This isn't the first time that Humphrey has caused a stir with his podcast. One month ago, Humphrey said safety Kyle Hamilton "knew" he was going to make a game-sealing interception of Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa once he replaced injured starter Michael Penix Jr . in overtime. Hamilton later shot down that characterization, describing Humphrey's account as "pretty hyperbolic." "I think Marlon is very unapologetically himself," Hamilton said Wednesday. "He can be slightly abrasive at times, but that's just him. And talking to his family has always been like that. But we all love Marlon and we appreciate everything he's done for us [and] will do for us. And he's one of us." Humphrey has been a target of fan criticism over the past two seasons. He has been frequently booed during home games at M&T Bank Stadium. During the "Monday Night Football" broadcast two days ago, when the Ravens were losing to the winless Chargers, fans could be heard shouting "F--- Marlon Humphrey" as they exited the stadium. "I love the city. I think I've expressed this many times," Humphrey said. "I want to win in front of the fans just because it's not cheap to be in those seats." Has the fans' negativity toward him affected his view of them? "To answer your question," Humphrey replied, "nothing has changed how I feel."

stories.title: 2027 UFL Draft tracker, results, top prospects as Diego Pavia finds landing spot
stories.summary: Diego Pavia is among those waiting to hear his name called during the 2027 UFL Draft. Here are the full results from the spring football draft.
stories.detailText: The 2027 UFL Draft has arrived, and football fans have one question on their minds heading into the event. Where will former Vanderbilt quarterback Diego Pavia land? Pavia announced in October he was planning to join the UFL ahead of its 2027 season. The 2025 Heisman Trophy runner-up will instantly become one of the spring football league's biggest stars and will look to prove to all the teams that passed on him in the 2026 NFL Draft that he deserves a chance to play professionally. While Pavia is the marquee name in the 2027 UFL Draft's player pool, there are plenty of other players with whom football fans will be familiar. A total of 120 players will be selected across the two-day, 15-round event that will help fill out the rosters of the UFL's eight current teams. Of course, not every player selected is guaranteed to play in the UFL. The spring football draft is a rights draft, meaning teams retain the rights to negotiate with selected players should they choose to play in the UFL. Still, spring football fans will be eager to see the crop of talent that could be poised to enter the UFL ahead of its 2027 season. USA TODAY Sports is tracking the results of the 2027 UFL Draft. Follow along with the latest picks and a breakdown of the top prospects available in this year's draft class. 2027 UFL Draft results Round 1 Columbus Aviators: QB Diego Pavia, Vanderbilt Colorado Stampede: Edge Xavier Thomas, Clemson Rhode Island Breakers: Edge Jahfari Harvey, SMU Dallas Renegades: CB Jalen Kimber, Penn State St. Louis Battlehawks: OT Isaiah Jatta, BYU Orlando Storm: OT Ricky Lee, North Carolina A&T DC Defenders: OT Aamil Wagner, Notre Dame Louisville Kings: OT Dalton Wagner, Arkansas Round 2 Columbus Aviators: WR Tru Edwards, Louisiana Tech Rhode Island Breakers: OT Jeremiah Byers, Florida State Dallas Renegades: Edge Marvin Jones Jr., Oklahoma Colorado Stampede: CB Latrell McCutchin, Houston St. Louis Battlehawks: OT Derrick Graham, Tulane Orlando Storm: Edge Jalan Gaines, Illinois State DC Defenders: WR Malik Cunningham, Louisville Louisville Kings: OL Corey Robinson, Arkansas 2027 UFL Draft top prospects QB Diego Pavia Pavia starred across two seasons at Vanderbilt, leading the Commodores to a winning record in back-to-back seasons. That included a 10-3 mark in 2025, a season during which he completed 70.6% of his passes for 3,539 yards, 29 touchdowns and eight interceptions while adding 862 yards and 10 touchdowns on the ground. Pavia finished as the runner-up in the 2025 Heisman Trophy voting and signed with the Baltimore Ravens after going undrafted in the 2026 NFL Draft. He was released before the preseason and now will look for a shot to play in the UFL. QB Adrian Martinez Martinez played spring football in 2024, when he won the USFL MVP while a member of the Birmingham Stallions after throwing for 1,748 yards, 15 touchdowns and three interceptions while adding a league-high 528 rushing yards and three scores on the ground. He parlayed that opportunity into a chance with the New York Jets and has spent the last three NFL seasons with the Jets, San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks. Currently, Martinez is on the Seahawks' practice squad. It isn't clear whether the 26-year-old will look to return to spring football, but his dual-threat ability will certainly make him a hot commodity should he decide to do so. RB Carson Steele Steele went undrafted out of UCLA in 2024 but quickly earned a role in the Kansas City Chiefs' backfield. He totaled 183 yards on 56 carries as a rookie but has only handled one touch, a 4-yard reception, over his last two years with the Chiefs and the Philadelphia Eagles. Steele (6-0, 228 pounds) is a big-bodied bruiser who runs with great physicality. That could make the 24-year-old a goal-line hammer at the UFL level. WR Luke Floriea Floriea may not be a household name, but he endeared himself to Cleveland Browns fans during the 2025 and 2026 preseasons. The Kent State product notched a combined seven receptions for 125 yards and three touchdowns across four games of preseason action with the Browns. Floriea spent the 2025 season on Cleveland's practice squad but failed to earn a spot despite a strong performance in the 2026 preseason. The 25-year-old is small at 5-8, 180 pounds, but his hands and separation skills could make him a quality UFL pass-catcher. WR Malik Cunningham Cunningham, a former Louisville quarterback, began his career as a signal-caller for the Baltimore Ravens and New England Patriots. However, in recent seasons, he transitioned to the receiver position and played one game at the position for the Detroit Lions. Cunningham, 28, has never attempt a pass nor made a catch at the NFL level, but his dual-threat skill set would make him an intriguing fit for the UFL. WR Jamari Thrash Cunningham isn't the only Louisville product who could draw interest in the UFL draft. Thrash, a 2024 fifth-round pick by the Browns, is in the player pool, and UFL teams would love to get their hands on the speedy 6-0, 190-pound receiver. Thrash recorded 13 receptions for 129 yards across two seasons with the Browns. He also spent two weeks on the Las Vegas Raiders' practice squad during the 2026 NFL season. TE Jaheim Bell Bell was a seventh-round pick by the Patriots in the 2024 NFL Draft after he enjoyed a standout career at South Carolina and Florida State. Bell made just two catches for 20 yards with the Patriots, but he showed off his upside as a senior with the Seminoles, recording 39 receptions for 503 yards and two touchdowns. Bell is a bit short for a tight end at 6-2, 241 pounds, but he has a well-rounded skill set that could make him hard to cover for UFL defenders. TE Dae'Quan Wright Wright's name will be familiar to college football fans, as he tried to become one of the first players to see action with an NFL team and return to the college level. His efforts were denied, leaving Wright in limbo after the Browns waived him and LSU chose not to add him to its roster. Wright (6-4, 246 pounds) may yet get a chance to play professionally in the UFL. The Ole Miss product had 39 catches for 635 yards and five touchdowns his final season with the Rebels and it's easy to see him developing into a mismatch threat in the spring game. G Shiyazh Pete Pete, like Wright, made headlines during the 2026 NFL preseason. The Kentucky product spent time with the Dallas Cowboys, becoming the first NFL player from the Navajo Nation and earning rave reviews for a locker room speech following Dallas' preseason win over the Arizona Cardinals. At 6-9, 309 pounds, Pete looks the part of a high-upside, developmental offensive lineman. Developing in the UFL could help him eventually emerge as a contributor thanks to his size alone. DT Brodric Martin-Rhodes Martin-Rhodes is one of the highest-drafted former NFL players in the 2027 UFL Draft's player pool. He was a third-round pick by the Lions in 2023 but was never quite able to carve out a role during his NFL stops with the Lions and Pittsburgh Steelers. Martin-Rhodes has just six career tackles and no sacks. The 27-year-old will look to show off his abilities as a run stuffer behind his 6-5, 330-pound frame. stories.title: Week 10 Observations: I Like That!
stories.summary: The Season’s Second Act Begins
stories.detailText: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 15: Kirk Cousins #8 and Christian Darrisaw #71 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrate a touchdown against the Green Bay Packers during the fourth quarter at Lambeau Field on November 15, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Vikings began the unexpected second act of their 2026 season with a resounding 30-10 road victory over the rival Green Bay Packers. Between Kirk Cousins’ emotional return and the defense’s historic season, it’s hard to imagine a more memorable and satisfying result. How could you not be moved by this? An emotional Kirk Cousins, in his return to the Vikings at Lambeau Field: “I tore my Achilles here and it’s been a tough three years…” pic.twitter.com/8PhbEVs7Oq — Lindsey Thiry (@LindseyThiry) November 15, 2026 The Daily Norseman crew did their usual stellar job recapping the rewarding victory here , here , and here . Aside from the obvious candidates (e.g., Turner, Van Ginkel, Redmond, Smith, Wilson, Van Noy, Price), I was particularly encouraged by contributions from Caleb Banks, Elijah Williams, Gavin Bartholomew, Tai Felton, and Jakobe Thomas. Maybe we do have some depth, huh? Topline Takeaways Like He Never Left. Kirk Cousins parachuted into Vikings practice on Wednesday and started on Sunday. As unheard of as that is, given the chaos that’s defined the past two seasons at quarterback, seeing him run out to the huddle for the opening series felt totally normal, as if time stood still. I was eagerly soaking it all in. Even with a few days of prep and a playbook that had changed since 2023, Cousins’ familiarity with the scheme and system was evident from the get-go. While the numbers weren’t overwhelming – 21 for 31, 207 yards, 2 TDs, and an interception – the eye test was passed with flying colors. Of course, not all passes and not all yards gained on them are created equal. How and when matter. That’s where Cousins immediately changed things. EPA per play improved (+0.04), and the Vikings offense converted 8-of-16 third downs. This included a 3rd-and-23 TD to Myles Price and a critical 3rd-and-12 conversion to Justin Jefferson, who also saw a season-high number of targets. Coincidence? I think not. This was a notable improvement over the 3-for-10 third-down conversion rate in the loss to the Lions and the 3-for-11 in the ugly win against the Colts. The Bills game? Let’s not go there. Drew Brees liked what he saw. Drew Brees with high praise for @KirkCousins8 in his first game back with the Vikings. @drewbrees 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/0hhdxTezwx — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 15, 2026 It’s also no fluke that Sunday’s game saw the Vikings’ offensive time of possession jump to over 35 minutes. This was a marked improvement over the abysmal 17 minutes against the Bills and 24 minutes against the Lions, respectively, in the team’s two losses. It was also much better than the 28 minutes in the ugly home win over the hapless Colts. It’s almost as if the mere threat of an effective passing game suddenly makes running the ball easier. Weird. It’s just one week, and time will tell, but based on interviews and body language, this seems like a different Kirk Cousins to me. One who is not only more confident and comfortable but also grateful for the opportunity to change the narrative of his career forever – something that seemed out of reach just days earlier. All made easier by what’s shaping up to be a historic defense by his side. I basically said it all last week: Cousins realizes the feel-good, storybook ending is within reach. Reports say the Raiders left the trade decision in his hands. He knows. This is his last, best chance. A Kirk Cousins with a Super Bowl ring would not only have a legitimate Hall of Fame resume (the statistics will be there), but he’d also have a statue outside U.S. Stadium to immortalize his role in ending the long-suffering anguish of a tortured fan base. I’ve Seen Enough. This Defense is Generational. After another impressive performance against a top-flight offense, it’s time to discuss the 2026 Minnesota Vikings’ defense in historic terms. While national media talking heads usually write narrative checks on the Packers that they inevitably can’t cash, it was worse coming into Sunday’s game because the Packers had won five of their last six, including a dominant win over a fraudulent Patriots team living off last season’s rep the week prior. Instead, they got another kind of check: a reality check. The eight sacks and four turnovers didn’t do justice to the torture Brian Flores inflicted on Matt LaFleur, Jordan Love, and the entire Packers offense throughout the afternoon. It was yet another piece of the puzzle that, when complete, could look record-breaking. oh OK, wow pic.twitter.com/iXMWXwyekv — Krauser (@Krauserrific) November 16, 2026 Points allowed through 9 games. 2026 Vikings: 126 1985 Bears: 124 — PowerTrip Bets (@PowerTripBets) November 16, 2026 The comparison to the 1985 Bears is impressive enough, especially given the changes made to benefit offenses over the past 20 years. Enjoy the rest of the ride, folks. Soak it all in, because this isn’t normal. It’s thrilling, but it’s not guaranteed to last beyond this season. Brian Flores will get another head-coaching opportunity someday, and key players such as Blake Cashman, Andrew Van Ginkel, Isaiah Rodgers, and Kyle Van Noy will be free agents. Meanwhile, Jalen Redmond is a restricted free agent, and it’s almost certainly Harrison Smith’s last hurrah. Third Time a Charm? Since 1990, the Vikings have made the playoffs 17 times, tying for 7th in that span. Not too shabby. Each year, the purple neurons in my brain lit up, distorting reality into something that justified the belief that they could not only make the Super Bowl but win it. My intuition has proven far more reliable. It’s equipped with the right defenses to filter out most delusions and purify it all. It shocks me back into reality, takes off the blinders so I can see clearly, and acknowledges the issues you know deep down will inevitably dash the dream. They truly aligned only twice: 1998 and 2009. Not 2000. Not 2017. My gut didn’t trust the defense in 2000 or the offense in 2017. In the end, both sides of the ball were an issue, but that doesn’t matter now. What matters is… things are close to aligning with this team again after 17 years. The convergence of multiple elements (i.e., the defense and Cousins’ return) for a magical season appears to be in place. There are still eight games left, so that could change before the playoffs, and that very well could happen. But I’ve never been as close to the long-awaited third instance as I was after this impressive win in Green Bay. A win, or even a razor-thin loss, to the 8-1 49ers next week will put it within arm’s reach. If so, let’s hope the third time is the charm and that the season ends with a third act, one that culminates in a Lombardi Trophy triumphantly lifted in the air.

stories.detailText: Wide receiver Mike Evans didn't travel with the 49ers for last Sunday's game in Dallas, but he was in Colorado Springs with the team as they prepare for their game against the Vikings in Mexico City. Evans remained out of practice due to the Achilles injury that has sidelined him for the last three games. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said that he hopes Evans will be able to get back on the field on Thursday. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw (neck, rest) was also out of practice and Shanahan hopes that he'll be able to work on Thursday as well. Running back Christian McCaffrey and left tackle Trent Williams both had rest days on Wednesday. Safety Ji'Ayir Brown (ankle), linebacker Luke Gifford (chest), cornerback Renardo Green (back), quarterback Mac Jones (illness), defensive end Khalid Kareem (ankle), safety Siran Neal (knee, foot), and cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder, neck) were limited participants. The 49ers listed cornerback Nate Hobbs (adductor), long snapper Jon Weeks (chest), defensive tackle C.J. West (knee), and defensive end Mykel Williams (hand, ankle) as full participants.

stories.title: Brian Schottenheimer has been unable to conquer this team problem
stories.summary: The Cowboys have the most penalties since in the NFL since 2016
stories.detailText: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images Penalties seem as old as time with the Dallas Cowboys. From 2020 to 2024, under Mike McCarthy, the Cowboys ranked first in the NFL with 570 penalties . It became a consistent talking point every Sunday with McCarthy at the helm and has continued under Brian Schottenheimer. The Dallas Cowboys have 212 accepted penalties over the last two seasons, the most by any team in the NFL. The gap between Dallas and the Houston Texans, who rank 2nd with 195 penalties, is the same as the gap between No. 2 and No. 16 on the list. (stats via @Stathead , @pfref ) pic.twitter.com/YiZvrq1UU7 — Brandon Loree (@Brandoniswrite) November 17, 2026 Penalties aren’t always the defining trait that makes a bad team. The Houston Texans are second with 195 penalties since 2025, and the Denver Broncos are tied for third with 193 . The combined record for both of those teams is 36-16. It’s the type of penalties the Cowboys have been getting—emblematic of what the last few years under Schottenheimer have felt like. On defense, it’s the holding calls or pass interference calls on a critical third-and-long that keep them on the field and the drive moving for the opposing offense. Dallas is tied with the Green Bay Packers for the NFL lead in automatic first downs (9) given via penalty on third down . The Cowboys also lead all teams with 22 penalties resulting in an automatic first down for opponents. The most defining penalty of the season—and maybe the culture of the entire organization—came versus the Indianapolis Colts, when DeMarvion Overshown ran out on the field as an inactive player. The Cowboys still led 20-17 at that point, but the 15-yard penalty set them back, and the offense ended up punting back to Indy, who tied the game on the next possession. Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown said he didn’t know going on the field last Sunday was a penalty. “I was just caught up in the moment. … I apologized to the team (after the game). It can’t happen again. It won’t happen again.” Overshown expects to play Sunday… — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) November 12, 2026 Then, late in the fourth quarter against the San Francisco 49ers, George Pickens got a taunting penalty as the offense is trying to score quickly and avoid wasting time off the clock. Instead of being at the 49ers’ 19-yard line, they got moved back to the 28. It took another six plays and a precious 42 seconds off the clock. Again, there are many reasons why the Cowboys sit at a 4-6 record. Penalties aren’t the only reason they are on the outside looking in as the playoff race starts to take shape. However, penalties signal an undisciplined team, and being the league leader over the last two seasons is starting to negatively define the culture Schottenheimer is building in Dallas.

stories.title: TNF: Texans rule out DE Hunter, RB Marks; Colts rule out CB Ward, starting OTs
stories.summary: The Texans and Colts ruled out several key contributors for their Thursday night matchup.
stories.detailText: HOUSTON -- Key players for the Houston Texans and the Indianapolis Colts will be out for their AFC South matchup on "Thursday Night Football." For the Texans, All-Pro defensive end Danielle Hunter is out with a hamstring injury after missing Houston's Week 10 loss to the Cleveland Browns , where they blew a 17-0 lead. That comes on the heels of Pro Bowl linebacker and team leader in tackles Azeez Al-Shaair being placed on injured reserve with a groin injury. On the offensive side, the Texans will be without running back Woody Marks , who sustained a concussion on a second-down carry in the third quarter against the Browns. Browns defenders Emmanuel McNeil-Warren , Sam Kamara and Quincy Williams collided with Marks, leaving him on the ground for a few minutes. A potential replacement for Marks is David Montgomery , but he has been out since Week 4 (groin). Montgomery practiced last week, and on Tuesday he said he's "trending in the right direction." He has no injury designation for the game. Wideout Marvin Harrison Jr . is also out with a hamstring for the second straight game. On the Colts' side, they will be without Pro Bowl starting cornerback Charvarius Ward , who sustained a knee injury in Sunday's win over the Miami Dolphins and did not practice this week. Indianapolis also will be missing both starting tackles, a concerning development considering the impact that Houston defensive end Will Anderson Jr . had in the teams' first meeting in September. Left tackle Bernhard Raimann is still being treated for a concussion, and right tackle Jalen Travis will miss his second consecutive game with a knee injury. Tight end Will Mallory will not play because of a hamstring injury. In the Colts' Week 3 win over Houston, Anderson dominated Indianapolis with 2.5 sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. He matched a career high with eight pressures in the game. Cornerback Sauce Gardner , who has been dealing with calf issues off and on since last season, aggravated the injury Sunday and is listed as questionable. Another injury of note is the toe issue that has slowed receiver Anthony Gould . He took over the starting role in the slot after Josh Downs was traded to the Kansas City Chiefs earlier this month. Gould is listed as questionable.
