stories.title: Chargers Week 10 PFF Grades: Del’Shawn Phillips lead spirited effort vs. Ravens rushing attack
stories.summary: Del’Shawn Phillips posted an elite game grade against the Ravens while former Raven Charlie Kolar topped the offense.
stories.detailText: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 16: Del'Shawn Phillips #53 of the Los Angeles Chargers runs with the ball against the Baltimore Ravens during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on November 16, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers beat the Ravens to move to 1-8 on the season. The 0-17 jokes and hypotheticals can all finally stop. Justin Herbert and the offense took a step forward with zero turnovers and a dominating performance on the ground with 160 yards, spurred by Omarion Hampton’s 105-yard night. Herbert also added 51 yards and a rushing score, as well. Speaking of ground games, the Chargers held the Ravens to almost nothing on the ground. All-Pro back Derrick Henry was limited to just 10 yards on 10 carries. The zero yards on the ground for Baltimore during the first half was a historic low for the franchise. You can’t be much more dominant than that. Let’s go ahead and check out the grades from Monday night. Offense Best TE Charlie Kolar – 74.8 OG Logan Taylor – 74.4 QB Justin Herbert – 73.0 WR Tre’ Harris – 72.0 FB Scott Matlock – 70.2 It was poetic for Kolar — the former Baltimore Raven — to catch the first-down pass that helped seal the win over his former team. He was also dyamite in the run game, posting the second-high run block grade with a 74.6. His 76.4 pass block grade was also fourth best on the night. Monday was Taylor’s best performance as a pro, finishing with zero pressures or sacks allowed on 27 dropbacks. His 81.1 pass block grade was tops on the team while his 68.9 in run blocking was fourth best. For the first time all season, Herbert did not throw an interception and it led to his highest game grade of 2026. Harris caught five passes for 86 yards all in the first half. Unfortunately he caught zero passes in the final 30 minutes of game time, but his yardage still gave him a new season and career high. During the broadcast, it was shown that, at one point, the Chargers were averaging 5.1 yards per carry with Matlock on the field and 3.8 when he was not. He’s done an excellent job as the team’s starting fullback and I believe the switch from a zone-heavy run scheme to a gap scheme has benefitted both him and Hampton. Worst OT Travis Burke – 39.5 WR Quentin Johnston – 52.4 OG Cole Strange – 53.4 WR Derius Davis – 53.6 WR Theo Wease Jr. – 54.1 Unfortunately the team’s first win of the year was also one of Burke’s worst performances of the season. He allowed a team-high five pressures and had an abysmal 27.9 pass block grade to go with a penalty. The next worse grade among the offensive line was Strange with an above-average 64.0. Johnston finished with one catch on one target for six yards. His season may be one of the biggest failures for Mike McDaniel in a season packed to the brim with them. The aforementioned Strange allowed four pressures and was also called for a penalty. His 57.3 in run block was below average but still better than Joe Alt’s 53.2. Defense Best LB Del’Shawn Phillips – 90.6 DT Teair Tart – 82.8 CB Donte Jackson – 77.4 EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu – 73.7 EDGE Khalil Mack – 73.0 What a night for Phillips, and also what a season it’s turning into for the first-year NFL starter. Phillips was a menace against the run on Monday night, helping the Chargers hold Derrick Henry to just 10 yards on 10 carries. He also snagged the team’s only interception off Jacoby Brissett when he sprinted under a deflected by Cam Hart. All night long, his high effort was apparent. Tart had his highest-graded game of the season overall to go with his season-high 81.7 pass rush grade. He tied a season-high of three pressures, as well. Jackson rebounded after a rough performance against the Texans to allow just one catch for six yards in three targets his way. Mack and Tuli combined for 15 pressures on Brissett with the latter recording a nine by himself. His previous season high was six in Week Three. Worst S R.J. Mickens – 25.1 CB Deane Leonard – 28.5 S Elijah Molden – 40.9 LB Daiyan Henley – 51.7 DT Jamaree Caldwell – 53.9 Mickens luckily knocked down the Hail Mary attempt by the Ravens to seal the team’s first win of the season, but it was otherwise a bad night for the second-year safety. His overall game grade was his worst of the year by far and his 26.6 coverage grade was very much the same. Mickens was also called for his third penalty of the season. Molden was credited with allowing five receptions on six targets towards him for 65 yards, including 53 after the catch. Henley also was dinged a bunch in coverage. PFF has him credited with a whopping nine receptions allowed on 11 targets in his area.

stories.title: Giants RB Cam Skattebo to nix backflips in wake of Aidan Hutchinson's injury
stories.summary: Giants RB Cam Skattebo said he is holding off on doing any more backflips after Lions DE Aidan Hutchinson suffered a major knee injury while leaping and celebrating a sack.
stories.detailText: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is retiring his trademark celebratory backflip for the time being. This comes on the heels of Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson suffering a season-ending knee injury while leaping and celebrating a sack Sunday. Hutchinson was placed on injured reserve. "It's hard to see," Skattebo told reporters Wednesday. "I'm saying, yeah, [no backflips]. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.' "That s--- ain't going to happen to me." Skattebo, the Giants starting running back, is coming off a serious ankle injury last year. But he returned for the start of the season and backflipped after scoring in New York's season-opening win over the Dallas Cowboys . He backflipped as recently as Thursday night in a loss to the Washington Commanders . Skattebo isn't saying he won't backflip again. The likelihood is he will. He has done it his whole life. But he mentioned after the opener that he might put the celebration on the backburner, before it reemerged in Week 10. Skattebo conceded Wednesday the backflip might resurface "if we go to the playoffs or something." The backflip was a point of contention throughout the offseason, even before Hutchinson had his mishap. Skattebo did his flip for the first time since the injury after hitting a home run at the Brian Burns Celebrity Softball Game in late May. Skattebo then stumbled while doing a backflip at Fanatics Fest over the summer, creating a stir. Giants brass had a conversation with Skattebo afterward. They preferred he didn't do it leading into the season, especially coming off a major injury. They didn't mandate he never do it again. "The big-picture message is you want to take care of yourself, take care of your team. Do everything you can do to be healthy, be back, be right, be good," Giants coach John Harbaugh said at the start of training camp. "What does that mean? It's not going to be the same situation the next time for anybody. It's going to be different. So, it's really the principle of it." Skattebo, 24, leads the Giants with 496 yards rushing and four touchdowns on 116 carries so far this season. Hutchinson, 26, isn't the first player to be injured while celebrating. Former Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica tore his ACL while celebrating a made kick against the Giants in 2001. But the current Hutchinson situation has prompted some debate about whether coaches should talk to players about celebrations, potentially banning anything that could be deemed dangerous. "No, I don't believe that," Lions coach Dan Campbell said. "I think what happened speaks for itself. We're not talking to 8-year-olds here."

stories.title: Browns roster seen as the best fit for one of the best 5 free agents left in the NFL
stories.summary: Could the Cleveland Browns roster benefit from an addition in NFL free agency? Leonard Floyd and Will Dissly could help
stories.detailText: As every Cleveland Browns fan knows, the roster is never finished being adjusted under GM Andrew Berry. That doesn’t mean every move works out or is even a big one, but Berry’s time with the Browns has seen consistent movement with the 53-man roster as well as the practice squad , including multiple moves during the team’s bye week . Cleveland didn’t make any moves at the NFL trade deadline, leaving concerns about the team’s edge rush and tight end groups to continue to linger into the second part of the 2026 NFL season, while the Browns compete for an AFC playoff spot . With the trade deadline having passed, NFL free agency looks a little different now. All players are waived, giving teams a chance to claim them no matter what their experience in the league is. Prior to the deadline, players with four or more years of service become street free agents with a chance to sign with whatever team they please. The Athletic put together a list of the top five free agents left on the market, with two players who could help Cleveland’s roster, including DE/OLB Leonard Floyd. Floyd was noted as a perfect fit for the Detroit Lions after they lost star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson for the season, leaving TE Will Dissly to be connected to the Browns: At 6-4, the Browns are perhaps the biggest surprise of this season. One of their top needs heading into the trade deadline was blocking at tight end. They did not make a deal. Harold Fannin Jr. is an emerging star as a receiver, but blocking is not necessarily a strength of his game. Dissly has been a proven run blocker over time with the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Chargers. He battled injuries in 2025 with the Chargers, leading to his release with a failed physical in the spring. If healthy, Dissly would fill a need for the Browns, who rank 25th in EPA per designed rush this season, according to TruMedia. Dissly was a fourth-round pick of the Seattle Seahawks in 2018, playing six seasons in the Pacific Northwest before joining the Los Angeles Chargers. A strong blocker, Dissly’s best receiving year came in 2024 when he caught 50 passes for 481 yards. Finding snaps for Dissly could be difficult for HC Todd Monken, with WRs KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston, and Jerry Jeudy alongside TE Harold Fannin Jr. and RB Quinshon Judkins getting a majority of the specialist snaps. stories.title: Steelers-Bengals on Sunday Night Football draws 21.519 million viewers
stories.summary: The game was never competitive.
stories.detailText: The game was never competitive. That didn't stop a huge crowd from tuning in. Via Nielsen, Sunday night's blowout win by the Bengals over the Steelers, 38-18, nevertheless averaged 21.519 million viewers. The Bengals took charge from the get-go, and never relented. By halftime, the Bengals led 24-3, and they had outgained the Steelers, 337 yards to 40. By the end of the third quarter, the Bengals had stretched the lead to 31-3. This weekend, the 7-2 Vikings face the 8-1 49ers on Sunday night in Mexico City. The game has massive postseason implications for both teams, and ramifications up and down the NFC playoff tree.

stories.title: Commanders, Cowboys get help from schedule in effort to chase down the Giants
stories.summary: The New York Giants have a winnable path in the NFC East, but they don’t have it as easy as their opponents.
stories.detailText: ) The New York Giants are leading the NFC East after 10 weeks of play, but the gap is closing. The Dallas Cowboys and Washington Commanders are hoping to take them down. There likely will only be one team coming out of the division for the playoffs, and the Giants want to make sure they are the ones that come out on top. Here’s a look at each team’s remaining schedule and how difficult it will be for each team to navigate. Dallas Cowboys (.477, 25th-toughest in NFL) Current standing: 4–6, second place in NFC East Remaining opponents: Titans, Eagles, at Seahawks, at Rams, Jaguars, Giants, at Commanders The Cowboys have one of the easier remaining schedules in the league, but they remain in second place in the division behind the Giants. They have very winnable games coming up, with the Titans and Eagles on deck, but then things get more difficult with the Seahawks, Rams, and Jaguars before the rematch against the Giants at AT&T Stadium later in the season. That three-game stretch before that rematch against the Giants could knock them out. Some wins against some powerful teams will likely keep them in the hunt and give them some momentum before facing the Giants in their first game of the 2027 calendar year. Washington Commanders (.467, 26th-toughest in NFL) Current standing: 3-5-1, third place in NFC East Remaining opponents: Bengals, at Cardinals, at Titans, Texans, Falcons, at Vikings, at Jaguars, Cowboys The Commanders’ win against the Giants on Thursday Night Football last week kept their season alive, and their schedule is about to get easier. After this week’s Monday Night Football game against the Bengals, the schedule gets much easier for the Commanders. They will play four consecutive games against teams that don’t have a better record than them, which could lead into a run leading up to the end of the season. The final three games are a bit more challenging, as they face two likely playoff teams on the road before finishing the season against the Cowboys in a game that could decide the division if the Giants fold in the second half of the year. New York Giants (.566, fourth-toughest in NFL) Current standing: 5-3-1, No. 3 seed Remaining opponents: Jaguars, at Colts, 49ers, at Seahawks, Browns, at Lions, at Cowboys, Eagles The Giants have one of the toughest schedules remaining in the league, as only three teams will face a more challenging gauntlet in the second half of the season. With seven games to go, four come against teams that are likely heading to the playoffs. If they were to lose all four of those games, they would need to sweep the Colts, Cowboys, and Eagles in order to get to eight wins. That might be enough to win the NFC East this year, but it is far from a guarantee. The Giants should want to beat some of these top teams to give them reason to believe that they can compete in the playoffs. That all starts with this weekend’s contest against the Jaguars, which is arguably the team’s toughest test to date. Kickoff between the Jags and Giants is scheduled for Sunday at 4:25 p.m. inside MetLife Stadium. Fans can watch the game on CBS or stream it on the Paramount+ app.

stories.title: Kellen Moore has run out of excuses in New Orleans
stories.summary: Sunday's loss to Carolina should be the breaking point for New Orleans.
stories.detailText: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 15: Kellen Moore head coach of the New Orleans Saints looks on during the first half of a game against the Carolina Panthers at Caesars Superdome on November 15, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images How many more embarrassing losses do the New Orleans Saints have to suffer before it’s time to move on from Kellen Moore? Sunday’s 20-17 loss to the Carolina Panthers at the Caesars Superdome should have been the final straw. This was a game the Saints had every opportunity to win. Carolina committed an incredible 17 penalties for 152 yards, compared to just three penalties for 46 yards by New Orleans. The Panthers repeatedly shot themselves in the foot, yet the Saints couldn’t take advantage of the opportunities in front of them. Instead, New Orleans dropped to 3-6 and watched Carolina take sole possession of first place in the NFC South. The Saints managed just 222 total yards, couldn’t establish a running game even with Travis Etienne Jr. back and scored zero points in the first half. The running backs combined for just 24 yards on 17 carries, leaving Tyler Shough to shoulder far too much of the offensive responsibility. At some point, the excuses have to stop. Injuries, personnel issues and growing pains can only explain so much. Moore is in his second season, and the same problems that plagued this team last year continue to show up every Sunday. And now, it’s starting to regress his promising young quarterback. The Saints have struggled with preparation, offensive consistency, overall execution and closing out games during Moore’s tenure. Those are the habits of a poorly coached football team, and Moore has repeatedly failed to find answers. New Orleans needs a change. Sunday’s loss was another reminder that this current regime just isn’t getting the job done. The Saints cannot keep wasting opportunities in a division that remains wide open. It’s time for the Saints to stop pretending things are going to get better without making a change.

stories.title: Fernando Mendoza’s painful NFL debut could hold answers to next test vs Broncos
stories.summary: The best thing Fernando Mendoza has going for him Sunday in Denver might be the same thing the Broncos have going for them. Both sides got a good look at...
stories.detailText: The best thing Fernando Mendoza has going for him Sunday in Denver might be the same thing the Broncos have going for them. Both sides got a good look at what happened to the Raiders rookie against Seattle. Presumably, both sides hit the rewind button. Fernando Mendoza (15) of the Las Vegas Raiders warms up before a game at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images For Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph, the attraction is obvious. The Seahawks sacked Mendoza six times in his first NFL start. Any coach with a rested pass rush and a home crowd willing to make life miserable for a visiting quarterback would be interested in how they went about it. For Mendoza, the part worth rewinding might come a second or two before he hit the ground. What did he see when he came to the line? What changed when he got the ball? And where could he have gone with it once it did? The Broncos present some big-time challenges in that regard. “It’s one of the top defenses in the league for a reason,” Mendoza said. “So they are very good, they’re very sound and I respect them a lot.” Coach Klint Kubiak is confident the rookie will process and adapt accordingly. “His approach has been excellent since he got here,” Kubiak said. “He’s a competitor. It’s his first NFL start. I thought he played well enough for us to win, especially in that first half, and we didn’t close it out in the second half.” A week ago, those were questions he had to answer against Mike Macdonald’s defense without the benefit of a single NFL start. On Sunday, there’s at least a chance Joseph asks him something he’s heard before. Consider what Denver can take from the way Seattle made Mendoza account for pressure. A linebacker walking up to the line gives the quarterback something to think about. Put one in each gap alongside the center and now the quarterback and his protection have some decisions to make. Michael Mayer of the Las Vegas Raiders avoids a tackle from Josh Jobe of the Seattle Seahawks in Las Vegas, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images The beauty of it for Denver is that neither linebacker has to come. If Mendoza hurries a throw over the middle to beat a blitz and finds a linebacker dropping into the very window he picked out, Joseph will have gotten what he wanted without sending anybody extra. So where’s the opportunity for Mendoza? Start with what happens if that linebacker comes. Somebody just vacated a valuable piece of real estate. A receiver breaking inside behind him can give Mendoza a throw he can make with his feet set, before the rush has much say in the matter. Six or 7 yards on first down would do wonders for an offense that spent too much of Sunday trying to figure out third-and-long. There’s a bigger throw available, too, if Denver decides to crowd the line and leave a cornerback outside with no safety behind him. That’s a chance to give Tre Tucker a ball down the sideline. The trick is confirming the safety really did come down. Seattle gave Mendoza firsthand experience with how much a picture can change between the time a quarterback calls for the ball and the time it reaches his hands. Getting Tucker involved would go a long way, especially if Brock Bowers’ ankle injury keeps him on the sideline. Tucker’s ability to stretch the field, and Mendoza’s willingness to take some chances on those long throws, could help open things up for the run game and the short and intermediate passing game. Tyler Linderbaum, left, Fernando Mendoza, center, and Jalen Nailor celebrate a touchdown in Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “There are a lot of variables and what our coach always emphasizes making sure we’re taking the positive gain,” Mendoza said. “However, those deep shots and those explosives are what can help us win the game. And so, I mean, it’s really play-by-play, and I look forward to taking a look at the shots we have this weekend.” Lost in those six sacks is a reason to believe Mendoza can make some of those throws. He completed 11 of 13 passes in the first half against Seattle and got the ball to eight receivers. He already knows what it feels like to take what an NFL defense gives him and move on to the next play. Kubiak can help him get back to that. Give Mendoza an early throw on a moving pocket. Change where Denver’s edge rushers expect to find him. And if the Broncos are getting upfield in a hurry, a well-timed screen gives those rushers an invitation to keep right on going. Some of which requires a seamless process well ahead of the snap. “I was very pleased with him getting out of the huddle, him making the correct checks, the correct calls,” Kubiak said. “That’s what he has shown in practice, his ability to do that and to be able to run the show that way. There’s room for growth, but in his first start, I thought that he operated the game like he does in practice.” Of course, there’s a limit to what anybody can draw up if the Raiders run for 65 yards on 24 carries again. Joseph had a bye week to study the Raiders. He hardly needed all of it to see the advantage in making Mendoza throw on downs when everyone in the stadium knows he has to. Denver figures to make the rookie prove he can solve some of the problems Seattle put on tape. Fair enough. But if the Broncos want to borrow from the Seahawks, Mendoza gets something out of the deal, too. Somewhere in all that film of what went wrong is a throw he’d love to have back. Sunday, he just might get it. “The most important thing is how he’s playing the game. We’ll coach up everything,” Kubiak said. “But like I said, and like I told Fernando, I was pleased because of the preparation that he put in. The things that he did in practice showed up in the game, and he’s going to have a lot of things to learn and grow from.”

stories.title: Chiefs-Cardinals Week 11 Wednesday injury report: 3 Chiefs starters miss practice
stories.summary: The latest injury news for the Week 11 game between Kansas City and Arizona.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Each practice day this season, the Kansas City Chiefs release an official injury report ahead of the next game. In Week 11, the Chiefs play the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon. Here is the Chiefs’ first official injury report of the week, courtesy of the team’s official website : Chiefs Starting right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) did not participate in practice and hasn’t since leaving the Week 9 game against the New York Jets in the third quarter with an ankle injury. During his Wednesday press conference, head coach Andy Reid said Moore “is making progress, but still sore.” Right guard Trey Smith (concussion) did not participate in practice after entering concussion protocol during the first quarter of last week’s game against the Atlanta Falcons . Running back Kenneth Walker (groin) did not participate in practice again after missing Sunday’s game and last Friday’s practice. Head coach Andy Reid will be cautious with Walker’s availability this week . Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods (neck) was a full participant in practice for the first time since exiting the Week 8 game against the Denver Broncos with a neck injury. Second-year defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) was a limited participant in practice again. He was activated from the Reserve/Physically-Unable-to-Perform list on Wednesday. Tight end Jared Wiley is not listed after reportedly fracturing his ankle in the win in Atlanta. Wiley was placed on the Reserve/Injured list to make room for Norman-Lott on the active roster. Wiley’s season is likely over. Linebacker Nick Bolton (shin) was surprisingly a limited participant in practice. Cardinals Many Arizona players rested on Wednesday, a sign of where the (3-7) Cardinals are after trading away Week 1 starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett weeks ago.

stories.title: Bears vs. Saints Injury Report: Kyler Gordon DNP, Jeffery Simmons Limited
stories.summary: The first official Bears vs. Saints injury report is out. @ryandroste with the latest.
stories.detailText: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Kyler Gordon #6 of the Chicago Bears reacts after an injury during the third quarter of the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears will take on the New Orleans Saints on Sunday afternoon, and we have both team’s first official injury report for the week. The Bears did not actually practice on Wednesday after holding practices on Monday and Tuesday of this week, so the injury report is merely an estimation. Even so, the injury report is mostly positive for the Bears at this point in the season given how clean it is. Just two players were listed with injury limitations, though both names are key contributors to the Bears defense. DB Kyler Gordon (shoulder) was listed as DNP. He had previously been hurt in the Bears’ win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the team’s last game. Reports emerged earlier this week that Gordon was not seen practicing during open availability. Head coach Ben Johnson has stated that Gordon is considered day-to-day with the shoulder injury. Only one other player was listed as on the report with an injury, and it’s a big one as well. DL Jeffery Simmons (knee) was listed as limited. At this point, it’s probably nothing to worry about as the weekend gets closer, but we’ll also be paying attention to his status as the week continues. Wednesday injury report pic.twitter.com/gVDIeno9Ij — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 18, 2026 Did Not Practice CB Dee Alford CB Christian Benford TE Dalton Kincaid OG O’Cyrus Torrence LB Dorian Williams None of these are particularly surprising. Maybe Kincaid. The Bills’ top tight end seems to be playing some version of “Spin the Wheel” when it comes to injuries this season. Weeks 8 and 9, it was a chest injury. Last week, it was an ankle. Sal Capaccio with WGR550 reported seeing Hamlin in a boot and using a scooter at the end of practice. Joe Brady says the #Bills are activating Tyrell Shavers off of injured reserve. — Jon Scott (@JonScottTV) November 18, 2026 What We’re Watching The Bills thought they solved their defensive back problem. Gardner-Johnson, signed Amani Hooker, got Dee Alford back from an injury, discovered versatility in Damar Hamlin, and found that rookie Davison Igbinosun was doing well at boundary corner. Now they’re suddenly facing a shortage once again. Hamlin and Christian Benford aren’t a lock to play Sunday. Alford has to work through the league’s concussion protocol. The current uninjured Buffalo secondary would look like Jordan Hancock at NCB, Sam Franklin, Jr. and Jalon Kilgore at safety; Maxwell Hairston and Igbinosun on the boundaries. teamStories.detailText: Maxx Crosby addresses reports that the Raiders are trading Kirk Cousins to start Fernando Mendoza. When the Raiders traded Kirk Cousins to the Vikings during the NFL trade deadline , the general consensus was that they were punting their season away — even though they were 4-5. Raiders star defensive end Maxx Crosby would tell you otherwise. Maxx Crosby walking off the field following their loss to the Seahawks on Sunday. Getty Images Crosby spoke about the Raiders’ decision to move on from Cousins and make way for rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza on his podcast, “The Rush.” He said the team’s mindset has not changed. “We don’t look at it as ‘Oh, yeah, we’re playing for the future.’ No, we’re playing for now. And we’re playing to win now,” Crosby said. “That’s all you can do. I know the locker room and everybody in that building feels the same way, and we believe in him, and we’re gonna rock with him.” Crosby said the Raiders’ defense will need to help Mendoza as much as it can, while the offense needs to step up to help him “play good ball.” In Mendoza’s first NFL start on Sunday, the Raiders scored on their first offensive possession. Mendoza showed why the team selected him No. 1 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft. He dropped back to pass but decided to keep the ball and scramble up the middle for a 10-yard rushing touchdown. Fernando Mendoza rushes up the field for a 10-yard touchdown run against the Seahawks on Sunday. AP Photo/John Locher Coincidentally, the scramble featured shades of his fourth-quarter run in the national title game against Miami in January. It was the only score the Raiders rookie had in their 21-13 loss to Seattle, but Mendoza showed a lot of promise, completing 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards. Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza walking off the field following Sunday’s loss to the Seahawks. AP Photo/John Locher Crosby knows Mendoza has a chance to be special and also knows what he’s capable of after going up against him during practice when Mendoza was the Raiders’ scout team quarterback. “He’s a robot. He does everything the right way. He’s a great f–king kid,” Crosby said. “He’s extremely talented, he’s competitive, he’s going to be a great quarterback for a long time.”

teamStories.detailText: The Seattle Seahawks took care of the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, assuring themselves of a winning record entering the bye. It was a game of few offensive snaps for both teams in what was a tale of two halves, as the Seahawks controlled the second half while the Raiders weren’t short on time with the ball in the first half. As a result, the only players who played north of 50 offensive snaps for Seattle were Drew Lock, plus every starting offensive lineman except Abe Lucas. Seattle Seahawks Week 10 offensive snap counts Seattle leaned heavily on having 12 and 13 personnel sets in this one, with Nick Kallerup managing to outsnap Rashid Shaheed even after missing the end of the game with a minor ankle injury. Shaheed’s return also meant Tory Horton was back to a distant WR4 status with only 10 snaps played. Zach Charbonnet is the clear RB1 over Jadarian Price, so there isn’t nearly the time-share deal as we saw with Kenneth Walker and Charbonnet last season. By the way, Irv Charles’ three snaps were all on Drew Lock’s kneeldowns, so don’t get too excited there. He did his work on special teams with 20 snaps. On defense, what looked to be a long day for Seattle turned into a slew of three-and-outs for Fernando Mendoza and company after halftime. The Seahawks played 59 total snaps, with safeties Julian Love and Ty Okada, cornerback Devon Witherspoon, and linebacker Ernest Jones IV going the distance. The usual suspects are atop the snap counts list. Seattle Seahawks Week 10 defensive snaps One of the biggest things that jumps out is Dante Fowler’s snap count, which went up to 20 for only the second time all season. Beyond the raw snap total, his percentage of defensive snaps played was a season-high 34 percent. Fowler made very little impact throughout the first half of the year, but sacks in consecutive games perhaps earned him more playing time. Even against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9, Fowler was outsnapped by Mike Morris, but that was not the case this time. Uchenna Nwosu’s 27 snaps played in his return from injury is his third-lowest of the season, but his 45.8% snap share is the second-lowest ahead of Week 7 against the Kansas City Chiefs. With a bye coming up, perhaps Nwosu will ramp up and his playing time will normalize again. Lastly, Rylie Mills has played 55 total snaps over the past two games without Leonard Williams in the lineup. For perspective, he played 34 total snaps in 2025 and didn’t reach the 55-snap mark in 2026 until Week 4. He’s had his struggles throughout the year but the defensive line by no means collapsed with him getting a heavier workload. And now we take this week off and await a season-defining rematch versus the San Francisco 49ers in Week 12.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Raider Nation got its first chance to watch the number one pick in the draft. The Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback, Fernando Mendoza, got his first action on Sunday with a loss to the Seattle Seahawks, 21-13. Mendoza had a hot start, going 11/13 in the first half for 90 yards and a rushing touchdown. It fell apart in the second half, as he went 6/16 for 43 yards. Mike McDonald turned up the heat by blitzing every third down in the second half, leading to four sacks. One area Mendoza needs to improve is throwing downfield. When throwing 10-plus yards last Sunday, he struggled to find completions. He finished the game 1/8 for 22 yards on throws over 10 plus yards. Mendoza is known for his accuracy, but he threw plenty of errant passes throughout the game. He needs to tighten up his mechanics when throwing downfield. He also needs to get on the same page with his new receiving corps. Plenty of miscommunication led to inaccurate throws, especially on third down. Fans should expect Mendoza to fix this issue going forward. To succeed in the NFL, the team needs explosive plays. Hitting throws in the intermediate and deep parts of the field will accomplish that. If this becomes a recurring issue, the Raiders offense will have a long second half.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders finally unleashed Fernando Mendoza, the 2026 No. 1 overall pick, against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. A game that the Raiders would lose 21-13. Without rushing to any judgment, good, bad, or indifferent, lots of good information on Mendoza was gathered. Let’s break it down. The eye test For as long as football has been football, the most important test a player has got to pass is the eye test. Mendoza passed the eye test in the first half of the game when he was 11/13 for 98 yards and scored his first touchdown by running a quarterback sneak 10 yards to pay dirt. A simplistic overview, but let’s get more in-depth. Raiders really drew up the National Championship winning play for Fernando Mendoza's first career NFL TD 🤌 pic.twitter.com/NQlAkxCXdZ — NFL Memes (@NFLMemes) November 15, 2026 Against the champs, Mendoza came out swinging; from the outset, it was clear the moment was not too big for him. He was never rattled and did not make any egregious rookie mistakes. The hits weren’t too much for him to handle and the speed of the game did not overwhelm him. Throughout the game, he played with poise and confidence. Mendoza stayed within himself; once Brock Bowers went down, he remained playing as though he were 1/11 of the offense. Ball security Throughout his collegiate career, particularly at Indiana University, Mendoza always took care of the football. Through the process of getting sacked, tucking and running and taking hits from free rushers, he always secured the football. By his own account, when running the scout team in practice, Mendoza refused to practice putting the ball in harm’s way. Meaning he didn’t even want to practice placing the ball in positions where it could be intercepted. Fast forward to Sunday’s game and it showed. The only pass he threw that was moderately questionably placed was when his receiver was assisted in falling down out of his break. Accuracy, ball placement and decision-making were all traits Mendoza was exceptional at in college and so far it appears to have translated to the NFL. What stood out Mendoza’s ability to tuck it and run provided a wrinkle the Seattle Seahawks had trouble defending. Using his legs to get what was available on the ground was a missing element from Klint Kubiak’s offense. On more than one occasion, it kept the chains moving and both the crowd and offense engaged. Being able to execute bootlegs and move the launching point allowed Mendoza to have early success. Fernando Mendoza ➡️ Cody White for the first down! SEAvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/KmbkHKSAKr — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Moving around in the pocket and evading the rush was clearly upgraded by inserting Mendoza into the lineup. Not just sliding in the pocket, but being able to muscle out of a collapsed pocket and still be able to keep his eyes downfield. He made one play, spinning out of trouble, rolling out and then hitting Cody White on a nice sideline pass to keep the chains moving Mendoza’s best trait in the passing game was going through his progressions and getting to his checkdowns quickly. We have seen veteran and even playoff quarterbacks be one-to-two read quarterbacks, then play hero ball. Mendoza wasn’t one of them. All week long, the message was that he was 1/11th of the offense and that’s what they stuck to. He hit his checkdowns after establishing that his other reads were covered in an efficient manner. Never committing the cardinal sin of staring down receivers or leading defenders to the ball. Another of the many quality things done was no hospital balls thrown against a head-hunting defense. Things to improve on The Seahawks defense finished the day with six sacks and got to the quarterback in completely inexcusable ways. Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon, known for his slot/nickel blitzes, tallied three sacks on the day. It wasn’t just that he got the sacks; no offensive member laid a finger on him; he came free and clear. Fernando Mendoza told @MikeSilver that this Devon Witherspoon sack was his "In a Blender" moment from his first NFL start. Seattle shows overload blitz to the weak side, so Mendoza checks the protection to slide that way. But the look was Mike Macdonald preying on his… https://t.co/EAidYAbHgF pic.twitter.com/pnauK0PyDC — Sam Warren (@samwarren83) November 16, 2026 Mendoza, moving forward, is going to need to be more cognizant of his own pass protection. The entire line was struggling mightily, and the overloads/unaccounted for rushers are most certainly something he’s going to see repeatedly. Which is something he acknowledged he needed to get better at speaking to the media after the game. Without Bowers, the offense was brought to a halt. Having four of six second-half drives end in negative yards and 27 yards of total offense in the second half isn’t going to cut it. Now, to be fair, blame isn’t being placed on Mendoza. While he most certainly has his part to play, the atrocious blocking, running and route running did him no favors either. Final thoughts An impressive early showing gave way to positive signs for the future. No one should have expected a rookie making his first start to topple the defending champions by himself. The least impressive yet most effective thing was Mendoza not digging a deeper and deeper hole trying to do too much. There were plenty of wow plays; not many went for huge gains or points. But they were impactful and kept the chains moving in situations where the offense needed a spark. Getting this experience against one of the best defenses the NFL has to offer should be priceless to a film junkie such as Mendoza. Following it up with a couple more tough defenses in Denver and Cleveland will make him better, as long as it doesn’t break him. Raider Nation, be patient. Mendoza is the future and with a properly built team around him, the future is bright.
